maps.signal_flow: The supervisor does not generate trading signals itself — it is the scheduler that fires each lane's paper cycle. Boot path: docker-compose backend runs `wait_for_db → alembic upgrade head → uvicorn main:app`; FastAPI lifespan (backend/main.py:66-311) starts (in order) loop-lag monitor, Redis, broker session restore, tick router + live_candle_store + quote_bus, paper_strategy_agent.start() and commodity_strategy_agent.start() (each wait_for 60s), bootstrap_paper_trading_runtime() (backend/core/paper_bootstrap.py:10-76 — forces paper trading mode, recovers NSE/commodity agent state, respects persisted kill-switch/manual-restart flags, auto-restarts agent loops, and fire-and-forget prewarms market-intelligence (90s cap) + commodity watchlists (45s caps) when a broker is ready), then RL trainer, then market_hours_paper_supervisor.start() (main.py:217). The supervisor (backend/core/market_hours_paper_supervisor.py) builds 10 RunnerConfigs in _default_runners() (lines 546-670): market_intelligence 60s, auction_intelligence 180s, fractal_market_profile 300s, directional_options 60s, directional_positioning 3600s, commodity_mp_history 21600s (timeout 420s), macd_refined 1800s (timeout 1200s), cbe_scanner 3600s, cbe_marks 300s, gann_tp_delta 60s (falls back to DIRECTIONAL_OPTIONS interval). Loop (lines 693-716): every pass calls run_due_once() which, under a single asyncio.Lock, splits enabled+not-running runners into (a) due runners — per-runner market-hours gate true AND now-last_started_at >= interval — and (b) post-close catch-up runners — market closed, NSE session exists today, time >= 15:35, post_close_catchup=True, and either no success today (recovery-only default) or last_post_close_success_date < today (post_close_force_daily: directional_positioning, cbe_scanner — a guaranteed once-per-session EOD pass). Ordering: _run_due_runners (794-810) awaits market_intelligence FIRST and alone, then asyncio.gather()s all other due runners concurrently; the same MI-first ordering applies to the catch-up batch, after which paper_trade_recorder.snapshot_daily() records the EOD portfolio snapshot and successful catch-up runners get last_post_close_success_date stamped (761-782). Market-hours gates per runner: NSE-only for market_intelligence/auction/directional_options/directional_positioning/macd_refined/cbe_scanner/cbe_marks; MCX-only for commodity_mp_history; NSE-or-MCX ("gann hours") for fractal_market_profile and gann_tp_delta (via core/trading_calendar: NSE 09:15-15:30, MCX two sessions incl. evening, with 2026 holiday lists). directional_options, macd_refined, cbe_marks set post_close_catchup=False (never fire outside their session — no entries on the frozen post-close heartbeat). Failure handling (_run_runner, 812-881): callback wrapped in wait_for(timeout = per-runner override or global 300s); timeout raises RuntimeError recorded as last_error; a returned dict with status in {error, failed, timeout, broker_not_ready} is ALSO treated as failure; success/failure both emit a deduped audit event (_emit_scan_audit, 889-998 — emits only on actionable>0, fingerprint change, error, or 30-min heartbeat) and a scan-duration metric. Where paper orders happen: inside each lane's callback (fmp_service.record_paper_snapshot, directional_service.record_paper_snapshot, macd_refined_service.run_live_cycle(allow_entries=True), run_cbe_scan, gann run_paper_agent_once, auction run_market_hours_cycle); market_intelligence only refreshes NSE runtime data that S1/S2 signal generation consumes.
maps.cadence: Loop sleeps max(MARKET_HOURS_SUPERVISOR_LOOP_SECONDS=15, 5) between passes while ANY enabled runner's exchange is open; otherwise sleeps min(seconds-to-earliest-next-open, 300) with a 60s floor (lines 693-710). Per-runner budget: global wait_for ceiling 300s (MARKET_HOURS_SUPERVISOR_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS), overridden to 420s for commodity_mp_history and 1200s for macd_refined (inner self-timeout 1140s); several callbacks carry their own inner wait_for budgets (cbe_scanner 180s, cbe_marks 60s, gann 120s, directional_positioning 30s+180s/underlying, commodity_mp 120s/root+120s baselines). On overrun the callback is cancelled and recorded as last_error ("runner exceeded Ns timeout — killed to protect the supervisor loop", line 824-826); there is no retry/backoff — the runner simply becomes due again one interval after its last_started_at (interval measured start-to-start, so a runner slower than its interval re-fires immediately on the next pass; the `running` flag prevents overlap). CRITICAL cadence property: run_due_once AWAITS the whole due batch (MI serially first, then gather), so the next scheduling pass cannot start until the SLOWEST due runner finishes — a full macd_refined cycle (up to 1140-1200s) stalls every 60s-cadence lane (market_intelligence, directional, gann) for the duration. Post-close catch-up runs are NOT interval-gated: once eligible (>=15:35 on an NSE session day) a failing catch-up runner re-fires on every 15s pass (while MCX keeps the loop hot until ~23:30) until it succeeds or the date rolls.

maps.signal_flow: ORCHESTRATION: PaperStrategyAgent (strategy_agent.py:657) is NOT a supervisor runner — main.py:192 starts its own asyncio loop (_loop, strategy_agent.py:1040) at scan_interval_seconds=60; run_once (strategy_agent.py:2203) is lock-guarded and non-reentrant. Only the S1 lane agent is registered (_Strategy1LaneAgent, strategy_agent.py:511); the S2 lane was deleted from _strategy_agents on 2026-06-02 (strategy_agent.py:678-689) though its runtime still deserializes. WATCHLIST BUILD (run_once): market-hours gate via trading_calendar → data-quality gate (blocks only when overall='critical' AND symbol_count>0, strategy_agent.py:2336) → broker-ready gate (local-only mode flags MARKET_INTELLIGENCE_STRATEGY_LOCAL_ONLY/PAPER_TRADING_ONLY both default False → broker mode) → S1 monthly scan windows (get_all_strategy1_scan_windows; physical-delivery window prev_expiry−7 → expiry−7, auto-rolls to next month) → ATM watchlist fetched concurrently per candidate monthly expiry + broker-default + S2 native index weekly/monthly requests (strategy_agent.py:2413-2458), merged one-row-per-underlying with monthly preferred; S2 composite rows ('NIFTY:weekly'/'NIFTY:monthly') then REPLACE the plain index rows (strategy_agent.py:2489-2507) and flow into S1's scan. MACD MATH (two layers): (a) the 30m 'current' MACD(12,26,9)+RSI is computed by the market-intelligence-driven ATMWatchlistService._load_technicals (atm_watchlist.py:1883) on 30-min option_premium_candles closes (limit 80) PLUS a synthetic forming-bar close from live LTP when it moved >0.1% (atm_watchlist.py:1902-1915), persisted ~per-minute into atm_option_watchlist_snapshots; (b) scan-side, _load_strategy1_recent_snapshot_state (entries.py:91) re-buckets the latest trading day's snapshots into 30m buckets (last row per bucket, 6 buckets) and _strategy1_side_snapshot (entries.py:310) pairs the live row's current MACD with the PRIOR bucket's snapshot MACD as 'previous'; (c) an independent TRUE 15m MACD per contract is rebuilt every cycle from 7 days of raw snapshot LTPs resampled to 15m RTH buckets in Python (entries.py:208-308, needs ≥36 bars). ENTRY (entries.py:457-1016, runs after exits): primary = fresh 30m zero-cross UP on the contract's OWN premium MACD (prev<0<curr) — same rule for CE and PE, each on its own premium (the old PE down-cross was an inversion bug, fixed; see comment entries.py:607-620); re-entry = 30m MACD already >0 AND fresh 15m MACD/signal-line up-cross (_macd_signal_cross_up, entries.py:46). CE is checked before PE (elif). Gate sequence per row: EXCLUDED_UNDERLYINGS ('IEX') → active window present → INDEX T-0 skip (trading_days_remaining < MIN_TTE_DAYS=1) → expiry within 3 calendar days skip → sides/MACD present → cross present → data-quality staleness check on the observed snapshot bar (source='option_history_30m', entries.py:757) → existing position: same side blocks, opposite side FLIP-CLOSES the position then falls through to enter the new side (entries.py:783-811) → position cap (max_positions=MACD_STRATEGY_MAX_POSITIONS=1000, effectively uncapped paper test) → missing LTP → IV: no hard gate, iv_size_scaler rejects only ≥90% IV, else scales size 1.0/0.75/0.5/0.25× by IV-spread vs market (iv_size_policy.py) → already_processed dedupe (signal_key=underlying:type:entry_kind → latest snapshot time) → spot MA context (informational setup label) → market-profile direction gate — BYPASSED by default (NSE_S1_BYPASS_MARKET_PROFILE_GATE=True, entries.py:361-383). NO spread/bid-ask gate and no premium price band exist (deliberately removed — 'ATM is liquid by construction', entries.py:825). Candidates ranked (setup rank, learning score desc, IV asc, strength desc), kill-switch blocks new entries only, learning risk gate can block, then _open_position for up to capacity. ORDER RECORDING (entries.py:1018-1241): lot size from row → option_history_service.resolve_lot_size → default; sizing = Kelly fraction (0.25/0.50 premium/0.10 cautious) × learning multiplier clamp[0.5,1.2] × IV scaler clamp[0.25,1.0] on equity base = max(total_equity, initial_capital) under MACD_STRATEGY_UNCAPPED_CAPITAL=True; min 1 lot, max 5 lots; PaperOrderBook.place_order MARKET fills INSTANTLY at LTP ± 5bps slippage (order_book.py:53,220-233) — no spread, no fees at this layer; persists to macd_signals, orders, positions, agent_signals(open) + Telegram + commentary. Raw observations/blocks/candidates are upserted to agent_signals per cycle (entries.py:687-755, 945-984). EXITS (exits.py:59-213, run FIRST each cycle): per position — 30m candles via option_history_service.load_candles (limit 80, allow_broker_refresh=True in broker mode, gap-aware TTL-bounded Upstox backfill) + freshest mark from a per-position UNION query over snapshots+premium candles (exits.py:282); cascade: #1 hard stop −25% anytime; #5 partial 50%-of-qty at +50% → PHASE_2 runner; #6 trail arms at +60% but is DISPLAY-ONLY (does not exit); macd_reversal_30m = premium MACD down-cross through zero (prev≥0, curr<0) closes both CE and PE intra-bar. Deleted exits: window_end, dead_zone, macd_death, ma20_pullback, trailing-stop (exits.py:9-29). There is NO DTE/expiry-day/window-end forced exit in the live cascade. Closed-market cycles run _prepare_closed_market_state (prepared watchlist + mark-only re-marks via _mark_open_positions_to_latest, exits.py:346).
maps.cadence: Self-owned 60s asyncio loop (strategy_agent.py:1040, scan_interval_seconds=60), started at app startup (main.py:192) — NOT under market_hours_paper_supervisor, so NONE of the supervisor's runner-timeout logic applies. run_once has no time budget or timeout; asyncio.sleep(60) happens AFTER completion, so a slow cycle (broker chain refresh per expiry + per-position candle backfills + 7-day snapshot pull) silently stretches the effective interval with no kill or alert. Overlap prevented by self._lock with early status-return (run_once:2204); exceptions are caught in _loop, logged, and the loop retries in 60s; state is persisted in the finally block every cycle. Scan timeframe mismatch is deliberate: signals live on 30m bars but the loop rescans every 60s — dedupe relies on processed_signals keyed to snapshot timestamps (see risks). Out-of-hours cycles take the cheap closed-market path; universe bootstrap + watchlist live_refresh run per in-hours cycle in broker mode; agent-owned spot sync every 30th scan with 0.5s/underlying pacing.

maps.subsystem: market-intelligence — the 60s data-freshness backbone (backend/market_data/market_intelligence_runtime.py, MarketIntelligenceRuntime.refresh_nse_runtime), plus its stores (option_history.py, atm_watchlist.py), routing policy (source_policy.py), and the adjacent research-sync backfill daemon (backend/data/upstox_research_sync.py)
maps.signal_flow: This lane generates NO trade signals and places NO paper orders — it is the upstream freshness pipeline that S1/S2 and dashboards read. Each cycle refresh_nse_runtime (market_intelligence_runtime.py:902) runs 7 serial steps: (1) SPOT GAP-FILL — 5 NSE indices, 10-day 1-min broker backfill via auction_intelligence.live._fetch_recent_minute_rows (Fyers futures/Upstox index with price-band + median contamination filters), upserted into underlying_spot_candles (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE); 600s cooldown, live WS ticks cover the intra-cooldown window. (2) WATCHLIST REFRESH (refresh_nse_watchlists:343) — expiry ladder via atm_watchlist.get_expiries(live_refresh=True); full-universe (~217 names) stock watchlist rebuild every 15 min (MARKET_INTELLIGENCE_FULL_WATCHLIST_REFRESH_MINUTES), with a DB-state override that force-refreshes when today's STOCK snapshot count < 50% of the latest-session count; the full-universe call busts the v12 Redis caches and passes force_rebuild=True so atm_watchlist's stale-row filter (rows older than today 09:15 dropped from prior_rows, atm_watchlist.py:984-1004) makes the background build refetch broker chains; index-scope watchlists rebuilt every cycle per index monthly expiry. Rows (ATM CE/PE pick + extended 3-ITM/1-ATM/6-OTM strike window) persist to atm_option_watchlist_snapshots. (3) INDEX OPTION-CHAIN REFRESH (refresh_index_option_chains:481) — 5 indices × 3 nearest expiries from fo_contract_catalog → adapter.get_option_chain (upstox first, fyers fallback, matching MARKET_DATA_OPTION_CHAIN_ORDER) → analytics (PCR/OI/GEX/max-pain) computed on a worker thread (asyncio.to_thread, line 1341) → Redis `oc:{symbol}:{expiry}` with 60s TTL. (4) ATM PREMIUM TOP-UP (refresh_atm_premium_candles:540) — builds a per-session "ATM-seen" registry (current picks + extended strikes, reset at date roll); pass 1 refreshes current ATM picks every eligible cycle with broker refresh allowed; pass 2 walks the extended window DB-only, round-robin from a persistent cursor, under a monotonic time budget (90s default) with an 8s per-call asyncio.wait_for; each call is option_history_service.load_candles(interval='3minute', limit=160) which reads option_premium_candles by logical contract identity (DISTINCT ON (time) with source-precedence dedup fyers_chain>fyers>upstox>else), falls back to atm_option_watchlist_snapshots LTP bars, broker-fetches Upstox 1-min → aggregates to 3-min when the series is sparse (<35 rows), stale-for-today, or hole-gappy (TTL-bounded 1800s gap guard), persists ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then canonicalizes timezones and applies a 09:15-15:30 session-hours filter. (5) LEARNING REFRESH — strategy_learning_service.refresh_scores() recomputes win-rate/expectancy/size-multiplier per (underlying, option_type, signal_reason) from agent_signals/agent_positions for S1/S2 entry gating; 300s cooldown. (6) SECTOR payload (10-min in-memory TTL over a ~30s VAR/Granger fit) and (7) MACRO overview (900s cache, refresh=False). Downstream, get_strategy_health (line 971) computes the readiness gates (≥50 underlyings, 10-min live watchlist age, 36h execution age, per-index spot freshness) that decide whether S1/S2 execute live, run on latest-session data, or decline entries; exit paths in the strategy lanes are unaffected by this lane.
maps.cadence: Runner `market_intelligence` runs at MARKET_INTELLIGENCE_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS=60 under the supervisor's 15s loop, NSE market-hours gated with post-close catch-up. It is deliberately run SERIALLY FIRST — _run_due_runners (market_hours_paper_supervisor.py:794-810) awaits MI to completion before gathering all other due runners, so every MI second is inherited latency for directional/gann/auction lanes that tick the same loop pass. Timeout: the global 300s ceiling (MARKET_HOURS_SUPERVISOR_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS; MI has no per-runner override); on overrun asyncio.wait_for cancels the callback, the runner records "runner exceeded 300s timeout" as last_error, and retries at the next 60s due window — note step cooldown stamps (_last_premium_refresh_at etc.) are written only at step completion, so a mid-premium kill re-runs the premium step immediately next cycle (the historical 94%-of-cycles-killed failure mode; now mitigated by budgeting). Internal step budgets decouple work from the 60s tick: gap_fill 600s cooldown; full watchlist 15 min (+ per-cycle DB probe override); option chains 60s cooldown (== interval, so it effectively never gates: ~15 serial chain fetches every cycle); premium top-up 180s cooldown → runs ~every 3rd cycle, bounded by MARKET_INTELLIGENCE_PREMIUM_BUDGET_SECONDS=90 (working-tree default; budget checked only between calls) + 8s per-call wait_for + 0.1s per-call pause; learning 300s; sector 600s; macro 900s. Observed (backend log 2026-07-03): typical cycle 0.4-2.1s; premium cycles 92.9-95.2s (slightly over the 90s budget as designed); cold-start 22.9s.

maps.signal_flow: Supervisor _directional_runner (60s, NSE hours) calls record_paper_snapshot(underlying, '5minute', 16) for NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX. That wraps live_snapshot (30s TTL cache, per-key lock): (1) load local spot frame (market_intelligence_runtime, 30s cap) -> FeatureEngine.build_frame (EMA8/21, ADX14, ATR, RSI, breakout-12, rv percentile; thread offload) -> RegimeClassifier.classify (risk_off/breakout/trend/micro_trend/exploration/chop; sets preferred_expiry_kind + delta band). (2) When DIRECTIONAL_POSITIONAL_OPTIONS_ENABLED (true in backend/.env), fetch positioning_feed.latest(underlying) from directional_positioning_daily. (3) DirectionalSignalEngine.predict: POSITIONAL view (active when flag on + feed row exists) — if feed is_stale return None (decline new entries, no legacy fallback); side = htf_up ? CE : PE (daily EMA20>EMA50 backbone); require positioning CONFIRMATION (CE: oi_build_bias>0 OR pcr_oi<0.9; PE: oi_build_bias<0 OR pcr_oi>1.2) AND vol gate d_atm_iv>=0 (None passes); emits fixed direction_score 0.5 / confidence 0.60. LEGACY view (flag off or no feed) — bull/bear momentum sum (ema_spread*180 + breakout + DI bias + momentum_3*12 + momentum_8*8), floor 0.001, confidence 0.42 + score*0.18 + regime_conf*0.28 (+0.06 breakout), capped 0.85; no hard confidence/regime gates (RL policy decides act/skip). (4) data_status execution_ready gate: feature frame non-empty + spot age and watchlist age <= 600s + watchlist rows>0 (with a local-DB fallback and a force-override to ready when any option snapshot rows exist). (5) list_live_contract_snapshots pulls latest watchlist row per contract (target side, expiry<=45d, nearest strikes, 54 rows) -> selector.select_from_live_snapshots (thread): front-expiry filter when weekly-preferred, per-contract BS greeks off snapshot IV (floor 0.10/ceiling 0.62), synthetic spread from volume/OI/moneyness, hard liquidity floors (vol>=150, oi>=2500, spread<=0.20; relaxed for learning sleeves), distributional p-vs-q metrics (trading/terminal edge, tail edge, PoP, timing fit, skew tax incl. 0.035 index-put tax) -> weighted contract_score ranking, top-12 surfaced. (6) fetch_chain_analytics (6s; Redis chain cache; PCR/GEX/DEX/25d-skew/OI-build) + ensure_chain_tracked fire-and-forget. (7) _policy_pick (thread): HybridDirectionalOptionsModel rule gate per candidate (min rule score 38, spread<=0.28, |delta| 0.12-0.92, dte>=0.2d, late-session guard) then DirectionalPolicy (BayesianRidge Thompson sampling over ~signal+candidate+regime one-hot+chain features) ranks candidates and decides act/skip + size multiplier {0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0}; rule-blocked best is swapped for best allowed. (8) risk.approve: risk_budget = equity(3M) x 0.5% x multiplier; lots = budget / (premium x 30% stop + fees); no premium cap; daily/weekly loss caps evaluated but never fed live realized numbers. (9) RAG context gate (always hard_risk_passed=True; can only flip approved->False with evidence reason codes). PAPER BOOK (sync_snapshot, DB-backed): journal every cycle; mark open positions via position_marks (watchlist latest LTP -> chain-cache LTP fallback); protective exits FIRST and immediately for both books — stop_loss at -30%, profit_target at +45%, expiry_roll at DTE<=0.8; then if not actionable: legacy positions close as flat_signal only after min_hold (3 bars wall-clock) AND 300s sustained-flat confirmation, positional positions are HELD; on opposite signal: legacy closes as signal_flip after min_hold, positional held (new open suppressed by one-position-per-symbol); same-contract+direction refreshes the row and resets the flat timer. New entries only when actionable AND allow_entries (exchange in session — Bug-A guard against post-close opens via the ungated POST /api/directional-options/paper-proposal); open registers with the RL policy (entry chain context), close deducts paper_engine.costs round-trip charges and feeds the net R-multiple back into the policy posterior. Close-reason distribution in DB: 61 flat_signal / 56 signal_flip / 27 expiry_roll / 1 profit_target — zero stop_loss closes to date.
maps.cadence: directional_options runner: every 60s (DIRECTIONAL_OPTIONS_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS=60), NSE session hours only, post_close_catchup=False (no after-hours entries on the frozen heartbeat). No per-runner timeout override, so the global 300s ceiling applies (MARKET_HOURS_SUPERVISOR_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=300; backend/core/market_hours_paper_supervisor.py:816-826) — on overrun asyncio.wait_for cancels the callback, the supervisor records it as a failure ("runner exceeded ... timeout — killed") and continues; the next tick retries. Inside a cycle each of 3 underlyings runs sequentially with internal budgets: spot-history load 30s, strategy_health 3s, option-snapshot query 4s, chain-analytics fetch 6s; live_snapshot results are cached 30s (so the runner recomputes each 60s tick), summary cached 60s. Per-underlying failures are caught and reported in the result dict; only all-fail raises. directional_positioning runner: every 3600s, enabled only when DIRECTIONAL_POSITIONAL_OPTIONS_ENABLED (true in backend/.env), post_close_catchup+post_close_force_daily=True (guaranteed once-a-day EOD pass after ~15:35 IST); _ensure_table capped 30s, per-underlying compute_and_store capped 180s; in-session passes are idempotent upserts keyed (underlying, date).

Positions persist in runtime/auction_intelligence/paper_positions.json. why-no-trade gate diagnostics logged per cycle (automation.py:223-261). COMMODITY LANE: CommodityStrategyAgent loop (30s cadence, started by paper_bootstrap) run_once (agent:2499): MCX-hours gate (closed -> _prepare_closed_market_state still refreshes everything, no entries); Upstox-preferred quotes with Fyers LTP fallback + rate-limit backoff; per symbol _analyze_futures_symbol (agent:2174): broker 2-day 1-min history, closed-bar filter, today MP profile via shared MarketProfileEngine (15-min TPO, IB=4, coarse per-instrument value tick, agent:2084), prior-session profile cached per (symbol,day) (agent:2131), 09:00-IST CVD/VWAP anchor, ATR(14) -> evaluate_commodity_mp_signal (commodity_mp_signal.py:858): entry triggers in priority open_drive > ib_break > failed_auction > lvn_fade; VA migration demoted to context-only (position-management input, never entry); gates inside evaluator: OF volume-coverage gate (>=70% of recent 15-min MP buckets must carry volume else all OF entries block, signal:1070-1075), per-instrument adaptive pressure-ratio gate on initiative triggers (|ratio|>=0.25 of learned median MP-bar volume, signal:1138-1155), day-type suppression (trend day drops counter-trend fades; balance day drops breakout triggers, signal:1159-1174), corrected 'textbook' lvn_fade absorption (large flow + stalled price, flag ON, signal:757-784). findings.title: macd_refined cross dedup lexically compares mixed-timezone timestamp strings (UTC vs +05:30), suppressing/refiring fresh crosses
findings.summary: macd_refined dedups zero-crosses by lexical string comparison of timestamps (live.py:608 `str(t) > last_sig`) while the series index is UTC (+00:00) from the parquet-resample path but IST (+05:30) from the broker-history fallback, so when a contract's series source flips intra-day the comparison mis-orders same-instant/later bars — suppressing genuine fresh crosses for the rest of the session or refiring already-signalled ones.
findings.evidence: live.py:608 `fresh = [t for t in cross_bars if last_sig is None or str(t) > last_sig]`. The series is UTC-indexed when built from parquet snapshots (`resample("30min")` on captured_at) but IST(+05:30)-indexed when seeded from `_hist_close_series` broker history (live.py:590). Live state file runtime/macd_refined/signal_state.json contains BOTH formats: ['2026-06-24 08:45:00+00:00', ..., '2026-07-02 11:15:00+05:30', ...].
findings.signal_impact: When a contract's series source flips between snapshot-resample and broker-history across cycles (happens whenever the parquet series is thin), the same instant renders as two different strings and lexical '>' gives wrong ordering: e.g. a genuinely newer bar '2026-07-02 09:00:00+00:00' (14:30 IST) compares LESS THAN stored '2026-07-02 11:15:00+05:30' → a real fresh zero-cross is silently dropped; the reverse flip double-fires an already-signalled cross. Paper mode either misses or duplicates the exact signals the lane exists to measure.
findings.fix: Normalize before comparing: store and compare pd.Timestamp values converted to UTC (`t.tz_convert('UTC').isoformat()`), and migrate existing signal_state.json entries to UTC once at load.
findings.verifier_note: Verified all three claims in the working tree + live runtime. (1) live.py:608 is exactly `fresh = [t for t in cross_bars if last_sig is None or str(t) > last_sig]`, state persisted as `str(signal_bar)` at :612. (2) Parquet path indexes on captured_at = `_utc_now()` (live.py:422/586) → +00:00 strings; fallback `_hist_close_series` → `_close_series_from_rows` (:471) does bare `pd.to_datetime(frame["time"])` on broker/load_candles rows → +05:30 strings; fallback engages whenever parquet series < min_bars+2 (:589), so source flips per-contract across cycles. (3) Re-read backend/runtime/macd_refined/signal_state.json: both formats live, including SAME-DAY mix on 2026-07-03 — e.g. "FEDERALBNK|2026-07-28|330.0|PE": "2026-07-03 08:30:00+00:00" and "ASTRAL|2026-07-28|1360.0|CE": "2026-07-03 09:00:00+00:00" alongside hundreds of "2026-07-03 ...+05:30" entries. Mechanism: stored IST "2026-07-03 15:15:00+05:30" vs later UTC bar "2026-07-03 10:00:00+00:00" (15:30 IST) → lexical "10:00"<"15:15" → real fresh cross dropped; reverse flip refires within the 2-bar recent_idx window. No compensating logic; this line is the entire dedup. Not covered by any known-baseline item. Cross-day comparisons happen to order correctly (date prefix), so damage is scoped to intra-day source flips — which the state file proves occur in production. Fix is trivial: compare tz-aware Timestamps (both sources are tz-aware) instead of strings.

findings.title: Directional execution_ready staleness gate bypassed by mere row presence — snapshot query has no lower time bound
findings.summary: During an intraday feed outage, the directional lane's 600s staleness gate is silently negated: service.py:579-591 flips execution_ready=True and clears degraded_reason whenever list_live_contract_snapshots returns any rows, and that query (data.py:210-215) has no lower time bound, so arbitrarily old snapshot rows re-enable paper entries priced off stale LTP/IV (off-session entries are still blocked by allow_entries, so the hole is market-hours-outage-specific).
findings.evidence: service.py:578-590: `if snapshot_rows and not bool(data_status.get("execution_ready")): ... data_status.update({... "execution_ready": True, "degraded_reason": None})`. The rows come from list_live_contract_snapshots whose SQL bounds only `AND time <= :as_of` (data.py:214) — no freshness floor, DISTINCT ON latest row per contract over all history.
findings.signal_impact: The lane's 600s stale-watchlist gate (data_status) is the designed defense against generating entries off dead data. Because any historical snapshot rows (day-old, pre-weekend) flip execution_ready back to True and erase degraded_reason, the paper book will select contracts, score them with Black-Scholes off stale IV/LTP, and open positions during exactly the feed outages the gate was built for — producing entry signals the strategy definition (fresh-data-only) says should have been declined. This is a regression-shaped hole in the measurement-integrity layer (baseline #9).
findings.fix: Only override the gate when the newest snapshot row is itself fresh: compute max(time) from snapshot_rows and require now - max_time <= stale_watchlist_seconds before setting execution_ready=True; otherwise keep degraded_reason and decline entries.
findings.verifier_note: Read service.py:561-597 — the override is verbatim as claimed: `if snapshot_rows and not bool(data_status.get("execution_ready")): ... data_status.update({..., "execution_ready": True, "degraded_reason": None})`; latest_option_time is computed but never freshness-checked. data.py SQL bounds only `AND time <= :as_of` (line 215) with DISTINCT ON latest-per-contract over all history and `expiry >= CURRENT_DATE`, so unexpired contracts' day-old rows qualify. The designed gate (_build_live_data_status, service.py:1037-1065, stale_watchlist_seconds=600 in config.py:161) is what the override erases — including shared_spot_store_stale, which option-row presence cannot vouch for. paper.py:256-257 gates entry solely on this execution_ready (`actionable = bool(signal and contract and risk.get("approved") and execution_ready)`) with entry_premium taken from the stale snapshot's option_price; no mark-freshness/kill-switch exists in the lane (grep: zero hits), and baseline #3's is_stale gate covers only the positioning feed (signals.py:58) — different gate. git log: block added by dc005669 'Reduce cloud app bootstrap latency and stale data blocking' (2026-05-08), a symptom-patch predating baseline #9's measurement-integrity layer — not a deliberate fresh-data policy and not fixed by any baseline item. Mitigation noted: allow_entries=False outside session hours (paper.py:242-246) blocks pre-weekend/after-hours entries, so the finder's 'pre-weekend' framing slightly overstates; the exploitable window is precisely an intraday feed outage — the scenario the gate was built for. Empirical DB re-check not possible from this sandbox (docker CLI and localhost:8000 both unresponsive/hung), but the missing lower bound is verified in source; CONFIRMED on code evidence.

findings.title: Supervisor head-of-line blocking: one slow runner (macd_refined, measured ~533s/cycle) freezes scheduling for every 60s signal lane
findings.summary: The supervisor's scheduling loop awaits an asyncio.gather over all due runners before starting the next pass, so a slow macd_refined cycle (measured 533s warm, 1200s timeout ceiling, every 1800s in-session) blocks re-scheduling of every 60s lane (market_intelligence, directional_options, gann_tp_delta) for ~9 minutes roughly 12 times per session — lanes due at batch start do run once concurrently, but then miss ~8 consecutive cycles until macd_refined finishes.
findings.evidence: _loop() does `await self.run_due_once()` before sleeping; run_due_once does `await self._run_due_runners(due_runners, ...)` which runs MI serially then `await asyncio.gather(*(self._run_runner(runtime, now=now) for runtime in trailing_runners))` (lines 807-810). macd_refined has `timeout_seconds=1200.0` (line 623) and its last real cycle spanned 15:22->15:31 IST (parquet mtimes in backend/runtime/macd_refined/volume_tracking: MIDCPNIFTY 1783072354 -> ZYDUSLIFE 1783072887 = 533s).
findings.signal_impact: Every 30 minutes during the NSE session, the scheduling loop is blocked ~9 min (up to 20 min at the 1200s ceiling): market_intelligence (60s) misses ~8 refresh cycles so S1 watchlist/premium data goes stale, and directional_options (60s), gann_tp_delta (60s), auction (180s), cbe_marks/fmp (300s) simply do not get scheduled — 30m-bar MACD crosses and directional signals landing in that window are detected late or on the next bar. This structurally violates the documented 60s-cadence promise the lanes are tuned to.
findings.fix: Do not await long runners inside the scheduling pass: launch each due runner as an asyncio.create_task (the RunnerRuntime.running flag already prevents overlap) and let run_due_once return immediately, or at minimum exclude runners with timeout_seconds > LOOP_SECONDS (macd_refined, commodity_mp_history) from the awaited gather and track their tasks separately.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in the working tree at backend/core/market_hours_paper_supervisor.py: line 696 `await self.run_due_once()` (serial loop, 15s sleep); lines 757-760 run_due_once awaits _run_due_runners while holding self._lock (line 721, so force-runs also queue); lines 807-810 `await asyncio.gather(*(self._run_runner(runtime, now=now) for runtime in trailing_runners))` — the pass returns only when the slowest runner finishes; line 623 macd_refined `timeout_seconds=1200.0` with comment "needs more than the 300s global ceiling for a cold-start cycle", MACD_REFINED_AUTO_ENABLED default True, interval 1800s. Empirically re-ran the mtime check: backend/runtime/macd_refined/volume_tracking has 216 parquets from the last cycle spanning 1783072354 (MIDCPNIFTY) → 1783072887 (ZYDUSLIFE) = 533s (Jul 3 15:22-15:31 IST), exactly as the finder claimed. No baseline item covers supervisor concurrency (fd5b5566 fixed MI's own runtime, not head-of-line blocking) and no compensating logic exists (no task-spawning, no staggering; commodity_mp_history 420s has the same issue). One correction: trailing runners execute concurrently inside the gather, so lanes due at batch start get one run — the defect is that no NEW scheduling pass starts until macd_refined completes, costing ~8 missed 60s cycles per occurrence, ~29% of the session at degraded cadence. DB/API corroboration was unavailable (docker exec and localhost:8000 unreachable from this sandbox), but code + filesystem evidence is decisive. Severity high for correct signal generation: it periodically reintroduces the MI watchlist/premium staleness that was the proven root cause of missed signals, and delays 60s-lane entry/exit checks up to 9-20 min.

findings.title: Gann time-stop counts 60s scan cycles as 'bars' — exits fire ~15x sooner than the 15-min-bar design
findings.summary: Gann time-stop increments bars_held once per 60s scan cycle instead of per 15-min signal bar, so the 26-bar (6.5h) time stop fires after ~26 minutes, prematurely closing 40% of live paper positions.
findings.evidence: agent.py:565 `position["bars_held"] = _safe_int(position.get("bars_held"), 0) + 1` runs once per run_once inside _update_underlying_tracking, and the runner interval is 60s (supervisor falls back to DIRECTIONAL_OPTIONS_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS=60; no GANN_TP_DELTA_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS exists in core/config.py). The lane's signal timeframe is 15minute (agent.py:98) and config.py:144 defines `"time_stop_bars": 26, # exit if held this long without +0.5R progress` (26 x 15min = 6.5h). findings.title: macd_refined cross dedup compares mixed-timezone timestamp STRINGS lexically — suppresses or double-fires fresh zero-crosses when the series source flips
findings.summary: macd_refined's per-contract zero-cross dedup (live.py:608) compares timestamp strings lexically while the series index is UTC-stamped on the snapshot path but IST(+05:30)-stamped on the broker-history seed path, so whenever a contract's series source flips, fresh crosses are silently suppressed (UTC times lexically shadow IST for most of the session) or an already-signalled bar re-fires.
findings.evidence: live.py:608 `fresh = [t for t in cross_bars if last_sig is None or str(t) > last_sig]` and :613 `self._signal_state[ckey] = str(signal_bar)`. The premium series is UTC-stamped on the snapshot-resample path but IST(+05:30)-stamped when seeded from _hist_close_series (option_history broker candles). Persisted state confirms both formats coexist: runtime/macd_refined/signal_state.json has 350 IST / 220 UTC entries (e.g. 'AMBUJACEM|2026-06-30|430.0|CE -> 2026-06-25 03:45:00+00:00' vs 'AMBUJACEM|2026-07-28|430.0|CE -> 2026-07-02 11:15:00+05:30'), and signals.jsonl has 382 IST / 253 UTC signal_times. Lexically, '2026-07-03 09:45:00+00:00' (=15:15 IST, later) < '2026-07-03 14:45:00+05:30' (=14:45 IST, earlier), so a genuinely newer cross is dropped as stale; the reverse flip double-fires an already-signalled bar.
findings.signal_impact: The lane's core dedup — 'signal once per fresh 30m zero-cross per contract' — is wrong whenever a contract's series source flips between snapshot-resample and broker-history seed (thin early-session data, cache expiry). Correct crosses are silently suppressed for up to 5.5 hours of lexical shadow, and duplicate signals are journaled/traded for the same bar, corrupting the per-signal record the whole lane exists to accumulate.
findings.fix: Normalize every series index to UTC (tz_convert('UTC')) in _hist_close_series and the snapshot resample before cross detection, store signal_state as epoch seconds or ISO-UTC, and one-time migrate/clear signal_state.json entries by parsing to aware datetimes and comparing chronologically.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in code and data. live.py:608 `fresh = [t for t in cross_bars if last_sig is None or str(t) > last_sig]`, :612 `self._signal_state[ckey] = str(signal_bar)`, no tz normalization anywhere (state load/save is verbatim JSON). Snapshot path index = captured_at = `_utc_now()` (UTC, line 49/433); fallback `_close_series_from_rows` (line 471) does `pd.to_datetime(frame["time"])` with no tz coercion and broker candles carry +05:30. Re-ran the data checks: signal_state.json = 350 IST / 220 UTC entries (matches finder exactly, incl. the AMBUJACEM pair); signals.jsonl = 382 IST / 253 UTC; and 23 of 570 contract keys have journaled signals in BOTH formats (e.g. HAVELLS|2026-07-28|1200.0|CE: '2026-06-24 08:45:00+00:00' then '2026-07-01 09:45:00+05:30'), proving same-ckey source flips actually happen. NSE session 03:45-10:00 UTC vs 09:15-15:30 IST means post-flip UTC crosses lexically shadow an IST last_sig for most of the day. No baseline item covers this and no compensating logic exists. Scope caveat: comparison is only wrong at source-flip boundaries (same-format cycles sort fine); severity kept high because the flip is routine at contract onboarding (~4% of ckeys already show it) and both failure modes silently corrupt the lane's core per-signal record.

findings.title: S1 already_processed dedupe keys on the per-minute snapshot timestamp, not the 30m bucket — the same zero-cross re-arms every 60s cycle
findings.summary: S1's already_processed dedupe (strategy_agent_entries.py:860) compares against the per-minute snapshot timestamp instead of the 30m macd_bucket (which is computed and carried but never used as the key), so the same 30m zero-cross re-arms every 60s cycle; while a same-side position is open the existing-position block masks it, but after any intra-bar exit (hard stop, macd_reversal_30m — which deliberately fires intra-bar — or signal_flip) the still-standing, forming-bar-repainted cross re-enters the SAME 30m bar, and raw-signal observation keys (also suffixed with the advancing timestamp) plus strategy_learning stats get inflated with duplicates of one cross event.
findings.evidence: entries.py:860 `if runtime.processed_signals.get(signal_key) == latest_bar_time:` where latest_bar_time = side_snapshot['latest_bar_time'] = `latest.get("time")` (entries.py:345), the raw time of the LAST snapshot row in the latest 30m bucket (`ROW_NUMBER ... ORDER BY time DESC ... bucket_rn = 1`, entries.py:130-172). Snapshots land ~per-minute, so latest_bar_time advances every cycle within one 30m bar and the equality check only blocks two consecutive identical cycles. The snapshot rows already carry `macd_bucket` (selected at entries.py:174) but it is not used as the dedupe key. Additionally 'current_macd' comes from the live watchlist row whose MACD includes a synthetic forming-bar close (atm_watchlist.py:1903-1915: 'Append a synthetic forming-bar close... so MACD reacts intra-bar'), so the cross condition itself repaints intra-bar.
findings.signal_impact: The documented S1 signal is ONE fresh 30m zero-cross per bar, but the dedupe cannot enforce it: while a same-side position is open the block at entries.py:789 masks the re-arm, yet immediately after ANY close (hard stop, macd_reversal, signal_flip) the still-standing, still-repainting cross re-enters the SAME 30m bar — intra-bar ping-pong between macd_reversal exits and re-entries. Signal counts and per-signal learning scores (strategy_learning refresh) are inflated with duplicates of one underlying cross event.
findings.fix: Key processed_signals on the 30m bucket: store `runtime.processed_signals[signal_key] = latest_macd_bucket` (already available in side_snapshot as 'latest_macd_bucket') and block when the bucket matches, so one bucket can produce at most one entry per underlying:side:kind.

Decisive lines: (1) entries.py:860 `if runtime.processed_signals.get(signal_key) == latest_bar_time:` with signal_key = f"{underlying}:{opt_type}:{entry_kind}" (line 685) and processed_signals written ONLY on entry at line 1156. (2) latest_bar_time = side_snapshot["latest_bar_time"] ← `latest_time = latest.get("time")` (lines 345-346), the raw time of the newest snapshot row inside the latest 30m bucket (`ROW_NUMBER ... ORDER BY time DESC ... WHERE bucket_rn = 1`, lines 154-170); market_intelligence writes snapshots every 60s, so this advances every cycle within one 30m bar — equality only blocks consecutive cycles with no new snapshot row. (3) The correct key exists unused: `macd_bucket` is selected (line 148/175) and even surfaced as `latest_macd_bucket` (line 357) but never used for dedupe. (4) Repaint confirmed: `current_macd` prefers the live watchlist `side.get("macd")` (lines 329-331), and atm_watchlist.py `_load_technicals` appends "a synthetic forming-bar close using the current LTP so MACD reacts intra-bar" — so prev_bucket<0<live_curr can flicker on/off all bar. findings.title: Directional stop/target exits evaluate against marks with unbounded age; chain-cache fallback never checks payload timestamp and overlay fakes mark_time
findings.summary: Directional stop/target exits (paper.py:314-341) compute returns from latest_local_option_mark marks whose age is never checked, and a stale atm_option_watchlist_snapshots row (no recency filter, data.py:373-404) shadows both the option_history fallback and the ~30s-fresh chain cache (consulted only when premium is None, service.py:300-313), so a positionally-held strike that drifts off the ATM watchlist rotation gets stopped/targeted — or fails to stop — against a days-old price, corrupting exit signals and the journaled R-multiples the policy learns from.
findings.evidence: latest_local_option_mark: `FROM atm_option_watchlist_snapshots ... ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1` (data.py:377, second query :396) with no recency filter, then falls to option_history candles `limit=3, allow_broker_refresh=False`. chain_strike_mark (chain_analytics.py:409-427) reads option_chain_service.get_cached and returns entry['ltp'] without ever checking the cached payload's age. list_positions overlay stamps `row["mark_time"] = _utc_now()` (paper.py:220) regardless of snapshot age.
findings.signal_impact: sync_snapshot's protective exits (-30% stop / +45% target / DTE roll, paper.py:314-341) compute `ret` from these marks. After a weekend, holiday, or watchlist gap the 'latest' mark can be days old — the code's own comment concedes 'with no fresh mark, latest≈entry → ret≈0 → no false trigger', i.e. the stop is structurally unable to fire exactly when data degrades, and a stale Redis chain entry is reported as a fresh mark (mark_time=now). Exit signals in the positional book are therefore generated (or withheld) from prices of unknown age, and the RL policy posterior is trained on those phantom R-multiples.
findings.fix: Carry mark age end-to-end: return the source timestamp from every mark path (including chain cache payload time), add a max-age gate (e.g. 15 min RTH) before stop/target evaluation, and record a 'mark_stale' journal state instead of silently evaluating ret≈0.
findings.verifier_note: Read all cited code. Confirmed: data.py:373-378/389-397 'ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1' with no recency predicate; service.py:293-313 falls back to chain_strike_mark only 'if premium is None', so a stale snapshot beats the fresh chain cache; paper.py:307-341 exit block runs BEFORE the 'if not execution_ready' return at :343, so the lane's stale_watchlist_seconds=600 gate (service.py:1037-1065) protects entries but not exits; mark_time is stored (paper.py:302) but never compared to now. Two sub-claims corrected: (1) chain-cache staleness is bounded — market_data/option_chain.py:19 'OC_TTL = 60' and :135 'redis.set(..., ex=OC_TTL)' mean get_cached can never return a payload >60s old, so the missing timestamp check in chain_strike_mark is immaterial; (2) paper.py:220 'row[\"mark_time\"] = _utc_now()' is in the list_positions display overlay, not the exit path, mislabeling ≤60s-old data — cosmetic. Weekend scenario is also benign (last-session mark is the freshest existing price), and the no-mark→ret≈0 fail-safe is explicitly deliberate per the code comment. Severity lowered high→medium: the live exposure is the intraday off-ATM-rotation stale-snapshot path (real and recurring for positional holds, per the known near-ATM-only tracker behavior), affecting exit correctness and policy training data in paper mode, not entry signal generation; the most dramatic claimed vectors don't hold. DB/API empirical re-check was not possible from this sandbox (docker exec produced no output; localhost:8000 unreachable).

findings.title: No alerting when a lane goes silent; a supervisor-loop crash permanently stops all 10 lanes with zero notification
findings.summary: The supervisor task (market_hours_paper_supervisor.py:678) has no done-callback/restart, so a _loop crash (line 713-715 re-raises) silently stops all 10 lanes; no staleness watchdog exists and the pull-based health check (system.py:462) can never flag a lane that succeeded once then went silent (a dead loop even forces auto_enabled=False, keeping status healthy). Nuance: runner FAILURES are in fact wired to Telegram via scan_cycle_failed audit events (audit_agent.py:104 → notify_event, warning ≥ default threshold), but delivery is a no-op in this deployment because TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/CHAT_ID are empty in both the container env and /app/credentials.json.
findings.evidence: _loop: `except Exception as exc: logger.exception(f"[MarketHoursSupervisor] loop failed: {exc}"); raise` (lines 712-715) — the task created at line 678 (`self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._loop(), ...)`) has no done-callback, restart, or notification path. _emit_scan_audit only emits when a runner actually RUNS, so a dead loop produces no scan_cycle_failed events. The pull-based health check is shallow: api/routers/system.py:462 flags auction degraded only `if auto_enabled and automation.get("last_error") and market_open and not automation.get("last_success_at")` — a lane that succeeded once and then went silent for hours reads healthy. Telegram notifications exist (notifications/telegram_agent.py) but are wired only to trade reports, never to runner failure/staleness.
findings.signal_impact: The most severe signal-generation failure mode — a lane (or the whole scheduler) silently producing zero signals during market hours — is invisible unless someone happens to poll /api/system/automation-status and reads timestamps. The 06-29 incident (94% of MI cycles killed for days, most signals never generated) was discovered by manual investigation, not alerting; the detection gap that let it run for days is still open in the working tree.
findings.fix: Add a watchdog: (a) done-callback on the supervisor task that logs+Telegram-alerts and restarts the loop; (b) a per-runner staleness check (now - last_success_at > k*interval during that runner's market hours) evaluated by an independent timer, pushing a Telegram/audit alert; (c) mark the whole service degraded in /api/system/health when loop_active is False during market hours.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in working tree + live container. Decisive lines: supervisor start() `self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._loop(), name="market-hours-paper-supervisor")` (line 678, no done-callback; main.py:217 is the only start call); _loop `except Exception as exc: logger.exception(f"[MarketHoursSupervisor] loop failed: {exc}"); raise` (713-715); system.py:462 `if auto_enabled and automation.get("last_error") and market_open and not automation.get("last_success_at")` — silent-after-one-success reads healthy, and loop death sets loop_active=False → auto_enabled=False → degraded branch unreachable. No `add_done_callback`/watchdog/heartbeat anywhere; no code compares last_success_at age to interval. Finder overstated one part: _emit_scan_audit → record_audit_event(severity="warning") → telegram_agent.notify_event (audit_agent.py:104) DOES wire runner failures to Telegram (min severity default "warning"), so the 06-29-style repeated-timeout pattern would now alert — except `docker exec nomadcurie_backend printenv` shows TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID empty and /app/credentials.json has no telegram section, so sends fail-open silently. Downgraded to medium: all per-runner exceptions/timeouts are caught in _run_runner, so loop-crash requires a bug in the supervisor's own scheduling code (narrow surface); the gap is observability-only and does not affect signal correctness while running.

findings.title: Positional side (CE/PE) trend backbone built from option-table-scraped spot with gap-days silently dropped, and staleness check fails open
findings.summary: The positional lane's sole side selector (htf_up = EMA20>EMA50) is computed from spot prices scraped off arbitrary option_premium_candles rows with gap-days dropped from the EMA index, and this is failing live: underlying_price stopped populating on 2026-06-22, freezing the EMA at 06-19 while NIFTY rallied ~1%, so htf_up=False (PE side) is served as fresh — the date-based is_stale gate and the None-passing d_atm_iv vol gate both fail open around it.
findings.evidence: positioning_feed.py:111-113: `pos["ema20"] = pos["spot"].ewm(span=20,...)` where spot = `float(chain["spot"].iloc[0])` — the underlying_price of an arbitrary contract's last 30-min option_premium_candles row (rn=1 'EOD' snapshot); days with no front-month rows are skipped entirely (`if front.empty: continue`, :88). _positioning_is_stale returns False on any exception (:177-178).
findings.signal_impact: htf_up (EMA20>EMA50) is the sole side selector for every positional trade. It is computed over a non-uniform day series scraped from option candles: a day where option collection stopped early yields a mid-session 'close', and a fully missing option day is deleted from the EMA index — both shift the EMA crossover state versus the canonical daily spot close series, flipping CE↔PE for multi-day holds. The fail-open staleness check means an exception in calendar logic silently serves that possibly-wrong row as fresh, so wrong-side positional signals are generated with no observable degradation.
findings.fix: Source the EMA backbone from underlying_spot_candles daily closes (canonical series, gap-aware) instead of option-row underlying_price; keep option data only for OI/IV features. Make _positioning_is_stale fail closed (stale=True) on error, matching the is_stale decline-new-entries design.

Verified in DB: option_premium_candles NIFTY has with_spot=0 from 2026-06-22 onward (06-23 had 546 spot-bearing rows yet stored spot=NULL — arbitrary iloc[0] picked NaN); directional_positioning_daily NIFTY 06-22→07-03 all spot=NULL/atm_iv=NULL/htf_up=f with EMA frozen at 06-19 spot 24042 vs actual close 24270 on 07-03; 2026-06-26 is a real NSE session present in underlying_spot_candles but absent from positioning (gap-day drop); is_stale=False since latest row d=07-03 is date-fresh. findings.title: Commodity agent runs full closed-market preparation — broker LTP + 2-day 1-min history + MP rebuild for 8 symbols — every 30s around the clock
findings.summary: The commodity agent's closed-market preparation runs the full per-symbol pipeline (Upstox quote snapshots + uncached 2-day 1-min broker history fetches through the shared UPSTOX_DATA_LIMITER + MP rebuild + ~830KB state persist) every 30s around the clock while MCX is closed, with no off-hours interval widening or cooldown — verified live on a closed Sunday; however, since the limiter window is a sliding 30 minutes and prep stops at the 09:00 MCX open, the cost is off-hours backfill contention and churn, not carried-over rate-limit debt at the next open.
findings.evidence: _prepare_closed_market_state loops `for configured_symbol, active_symbol in active_futures_symbols.items(): row = await self._analyze_futures_symbol(...)` (lines 2643-2653), and _analyze_futures_symbol's _load_history fetches broker 1-min candles uncached per call (lines 2215-2263); the loop sleeps a flat `await asyncio.sleep(self.scan_interval_seconds)` (line 2040, 30s) with no off-hours widening. Live evidence: commodity_strategy.json (848KB) last_run_at '2026-07-05T06:12:18+05:30' (Saturday, MCX closed) with message 'Market closed. Prepared for next MCX session: 8 futures rows.'
findings.signal_impact: All weekend and off-hours, ~8 Upstox/Fyers history+quote fetch sets fire every 30s and an ~848KB state blob is re-persisted each cycle — burning the shared Upstox limiter budget (8/s, 1800/30min) that option_history backfills and MI's premium top-up need at the next open, and adding steady DB/file churn, for zero possible signal output (entries are hard-blocked while closed). Rate-limit debt accumulated off-hours delays the data refresh that real signal generation depends on in-session.
findings.fix: Widen the sleep when MCX is closed (e.g. 300-900s, like the supervisor's closed-market sleep), cache _load_history results per (symbol, session) during closed-market prep, and skip state persistence when nothing changed since the previous prep cycle.

Prepared for next MCX session: 8 futures rows... findings.title: S1's 30m premium MACD is assembled by two different series pipelines — entry side (watchlist snapshot + synthetic forming bar) vs exit side (recomputed from load_candles) — so entry and exit can disagree on the same contract's MACD sign
findings.summary: S1's 30m premium MACD is computed by two divergent pipelines — entry uses watchlist closes plus a synthetic LTP forming bar paired with the prior snapshot bucket (atm_watchlist.py:1912-1916, entries.py:316-358, :623-629), while exit independently recomputes from load_candles closes with no synthetic bar (exits.py:75-133, :200-208) — so entry and exit can disagree on the same contract's MACD sign, and with no minimum-hold gate the macd_reversal_30m exit churns positions within the entry bar.
findings.evidence: Entry 'current' MACD comes from atm_watchlist._load_technicals (atm_watchlist.py:1911-1916): candle closes PLUS a synthetic forming-bar close appended when LTP moved >0.1% (`closes = list(closes) + [fallback_close]`), persisted to snapshots and paired with the PRIOR bucket's snapshot as 'previous' (entries.py:310-346). Exit MACD is rebuilt independently per position from `option_history_service.load_candles(... interval="30minute", limit=80)` closes with NO synthetic bar (exits.py:75-85, `macd_result = indicators_agent.macd(ctx=ind_ctx, closes=closes, ...)` at :133), then macd_reversal fires on `prev_macd >= 0 and curr_macd < 0` (:205).
findings.signal_impact: Same indicator, same contract, two series constructions: an intra-bar synthetic cross visible to the entry pipeline may not exist in the exit pipeline's candle series (and vice versa). Concrete failure: entry fires on a synthetic-bar up-cross, the exit-side candle series still reads MACD<0, and macd_reversal_30m closes the position within a cycle — churn recorded as a 'signal + reversal' pair that the strategy definition never intended; or a real reversal is missed because the exit series lags the snapshot series.
findings.fix: Make one series builder authoritative for the lane: have exits consume the same snapshot-bucket MACD state used for entries (or have entries drop the synthetic bar and both read load_candles closes), so a cross and its reversal are detected on a single consistent series.
findings.verifier_note: Verified both pipelines in the working tree. Entry: atm_watchlist._load_technicals appends the synthetic bar — "if last_close > 0 and abs(fallback_close - last_close) / last_close > 0.001: closes = list(closes) + [fallback_close]" (atm_watchlist.py:1914-1915) — and _strategy1_side_snapshot pairs `side.get("macd")` (synthetic-bar current) with the prior snapshot bucket's macd as previous (entries.py:329-331, :351); entry fires on `previous_macd < 0 < ce_macd` (entries.py:623-624). Exit: closes come only from load_candles (exits.py:75-85), MACD recomputed at :133, down-cross fires at :203-208. The exits.py:198-199 comment claiming macd_line[-1] reflects live LTP is FALSE — live_ltp is never appended to closes. bars_open (exits.py:151) is dead code; no hold gate protects a fresh entry. DB evidence (read-only): macd_reversal_30m = 31 of 47 exits in 10 days; CROMPTON 280 CE 2026-07-01 entered 09:21 IST with entry-MACD +0.121 @ premium 8.2041 and was closed 26 min later by macd_reversal_30m with exit-MACD −0.023 @ premium 8.2000 — premium flat but the two series sat on opposite sides of zero, the exact churn failure claimed. No baseline item addresses this. Severity medium is right: it corrupts signal semantics (unintended entry+reversal pairs, dominant exit reason) but does not disable signal generation.

findings.title: Watchlist Redis cache version duplicated: market_intelligence_runtime hardcodes 'atm_watchlist:v12:...' bust keys instead of using WATCHLIST_CACHE_VERSION
findings.summary: market_intelligence_runtime.py:418-419 hardcodes "v12" in its full-universe cache-bust keys instead of importing WATCHLIST_CACHE_VERSION from atm_watchlist.py:39, so the next version bump would silently disable the invalidation and reintroduce the stale full-universe watchlist the delete was added to fix; today the literals still match, so there is no current signal impact.
