The adjacent comment states the delete exists because 'Without this, a stale "ready" payload satisfies _watchlist_rows_are_fresh() and the BG build for stocks never fires.'
findings.signal_impact: The next cache-version bump (v13) silently no-ops the MI full-universe cache invalidation — the 15-min full stock-universe rebuild starts returning the stale cached blob, exactly the stale-watchlist failure this code was added to fix. S1's ~217-name scan then evaluates frozen MACD/LTP rows: no fresh crosses detected on stocks, i.e. quiet lane-wide signal suppression with no error anywhere.
findings.fix: Import WATCHLIST_CACHE_VERSION (or better, expose an `atm_watchlist_service.invalidate_full_universe(expiry)` helper next to the key-construction code) and delete the literals.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in the working tree (which is what runs via bind-mount). market_intelligence_runtime.py:417-420 contains the literals `f"atm_watchlist:v12:live:{full_universe_expiry}:all"` and `f"atm_watchlist:partial:v12:live:{full_universe_expiry}:all"`, and grep shows the module never imports/references WATCHLIST_CACHE_VERSION. atm_watchlist.py:39 defines `WATCHLIST_CACHE_VERSION = "v12"` and derives all real keys from it (lines 839-843), e.g. `f"atm_watchlist:{WATCHLIST_CACHE_VERSION}:{mode_key}:{selected_expiry}:{scope_key}"`. Cross-checked the other key components: `_cache_mode_key(live_refresh=True)` returns "live" (line 490-491) and `_scope_cache_key` returns "all" for empty symbols (486-487), and the runtime's full-universe call passes symbols=None with live_refresh=True — so the hardcoded keys DO match the owning module's keys today (live Redis confirms the v12 namespace is the active one: `atm_watchlist:expiries:v12:live:2026-07-07` exists). Not covered by any baseline item (the fd5b5566-family fixes added this delete; they did not parameterize it). No compensating logic: the delete is wrapped in try/except that only logs a warning, and a wrong key is not even an error — redis.delete on a nonexistent key succeeds silently, and the shared "ready" payload then satisfies the freshness check per the in-code comment ('Without this, a stale "ready" payload... the BG build for stocks never fires'). Severity kept medium: no impact until a v13 bump, but the version has already been bumped 12 times, and the failure mode is a silent lane-wide stale-scan regression of a previously fixed bug. Fix is a one-line import + f-string using WATCHLIST_CACHE_VERSION.

findings.title: Supervisor cadence config duplicated between getattr() literals and Settings: GANN/CBE_MARKS knobs have no Settings field, so env overrides are silently ignored and defaults disagree
findings.summary: GANN_TP_DELTA_* and CBE_MARKS_* cadence knobs are read via getattr() but have no Settings field in config.py (which sets extra="ignore"), so env overrides are silently dropped and gann_tp_delta is pinned to the directional 60s interval — while the gann agent counts bars_held per run_once invocation, tripping the 26x15-min time-stop in tens of minutes (74/183 closes are time_stop at exactly bars_held=26, e.g. 37-minute holds); the supervisor also carries a dead divergent 900s fallback for CBE_SCANNER (config actual 3600).
findings.evidence: supervisor:660-666 `interval_seconds=getattr(settings, "GANN_TP_DELTA_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS", settings.DIRECTIONAL_OPTIONS_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS)` and :650 `getattr(settings, "CBE_MARKS_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS", 300)` — grep of core/config.py shows NO GANN_* or CBE_MARKS_* fields, and config.py:41 sets `extra="ignore"`, so any .env value is dropped by pydantic and getattr always returns the fallback. Also supervisor:634 carries a second divergent default (`getattr(settings, "CBE_SCANNER_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS", 900)` vs config.py:251 `= 3600`).
findings.signal_impact: gann_tp_delta's cadence is permanently pinned to the DIRECTIONAL 60s interval with no operator control. gann's own time_stop_bars=26 counts run_once invocations, so at 60s the 'bar' time-stop trips in ~26 minutes instead of ~6.5h — the 183-closed/0-open churn signature — and the natural fix (raise the interval via env) silently does nothing. Duplicate defaults (900 vs 3600) also mislead anyone reasoning about cbe cadence from the supervisor file.
findings.fix: Declare GANN_TP_DELTA_AUTO_ENABLED, GANN_TP_DELTA_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS and CBE_MARKS_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS as real Settings fields and replace every getattr(settings, ...) in the supervisor with direct attribute access; delete the stray 900 literal.
findings.verifier_note: All three legs verified in working tree + runtime state. (1) Missing fields: grep of backend/core/config.py finds NO GANN_TP_DELTA_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS / GANN_TP_DELTA_AUTO_ENABLED / CBE_MARKS_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS; config.py:41 has `extra="ignore"`, so pydantic drops any .env value and the supervisor getattr fallbacks always win: market_hours_paper_supervisor.py registers gann with `interval_seconds=getattr(settings, "GANN_TP_DELTA_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS", settings.DIRECTIONAL_OPTIONS_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS)` and DIRECTIONAL_OPTIONS_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS=60 (config.py:224) — matching the stated 60s gann cadence. cbe_marks uses `getattr(settings, "CBE_MARKS_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS", 300)`. (2) Divergent duplicate default: supervisor `getattr(settings, "CBE_SCANNER_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS", 900)` vs config.py:251 `= 3600`; field exists so 3600 is used and the 900 is dead/misleading only (no behavioral bug). (3) Signal impact confirmed empirically: gann agent.py:565 `position["bars_held"] = ... + 1` runs unconditionally in _refresh_open_positions on every run_paper_agent_once — no new-15min-bar gating — while gann_tp_delta/config.py:144 sets `"time_stop_bars": 26` against `"timeframe": "15minute"` (intended ~6.5h). Runtime state backend/runtime/gann_tp_delta/paper/agent_positions.json shows exactly the claimed signature: 183 closed / 0 open, close_reason Counter {gann_stop:78, time_stop:74, gann_target:25, option_expiry:5, opposite_high_conviction:1}, every time_stop at bars_held=26, with wall-clock holds as short as 37 min (NIFTY 09:55→10:32 UTC). No baseline item covers gann; not deliberate (the config comment says "exit if held this long without +0.5R progress" on a 15-minute timeframe). Severity medium: correct-signal impact is real (premature time-stop churn + no operator control via env), but paper-mode only and one strategy lane.

findings.title: Directional lane's research path and live path are separate ~170-line copies: _score_contract vs _score_snapshot_contract, and _snapshot calls predict() WITHOUT positioning while _live_snapshot passes it
findings.summary: Directional lane hand-maintains two ~170-line copies of contract scoring (selector.py _score_contract:382 vs _score_snapshot_contract:571, with mirrored "same logic as" comments), and the research/backtest path calls predict() without positioning (service.py:379, backtest.py:154) while the live paper path passes positioning (service.py:518) with DIRECTIONAL_POSITIONAL_OPTIONS_ENABLED=true — so the workspace/backtester validates the legacy momentum view while paper trades the positional-confirmation view.
findings.evidence: selector.py:382 `_score_contract` and :571 `_score_snapshot_contract` are near-identical bodies (diff of the two ranges is only parameter-shape lines: bar vs snapshot field extraction, meta.strike vs strike; both even carry mirrored comments 'same logic as _score_snapshot_contract'). service.py duplicates the assembly too: `_snapshot` (:361) does `signal = self.signals.predict(row, regime, timeframe)` (:379, no positioning) and feeds the workspace/backtest (:130-136), while the live paper path `_live_snapshot` does `self.signals.predict(row, regime, timeframe, positioning=positioning)` (:518).
findings.signal_impact: The lane's validation surface (workspace + backtester) evaluates the LEGACY momentum view (the one measured at PF 0.2) while the paper loop generates the positional-confirmation view — research results shown to the owner no longer describe the signals actually produced. Any future gate/weight change applied to one scoring copy (liquidity floors, skew tax, learning-sleeve relaxation) silently diverges the other, so 'backtest says X, paper does Y' becomes structural.
findings.fix: Extract one `_score_candidate(fields...)` taking a normalized dict built by two thin adapters (ContractMeta->dict, snapshot->dict), and have `_snapshot` fetch/pass the same positioning feed (or explicitly label the workspace output 'legacy view' until unified).
findings.verifier_note: Read both function bodies in TradeBot/backend/directional_options/selector.py: lines 382-569 and 571+ are near-identical (same spread/liquidity/relax-gate/score-weight code; line 440 comment: "same logic as _score_snapshot_contract"). service.py:379 `signal = self.signals.predict(row, regime, timeframe)` (no positioning; feeds workspace():130 and backtester) vs service.py:518 `self.signals.predict(row, regime, timeframe, positioning=positioning)`; backtest.py:154 also omits positioning. signals.py:52 `positional_active = settings.DIRECTIONAL_POSITIONAL_OPTIONS_ENABLED and positioning is not None` switches to a different (HTF+OI-build/PCR) view, and backend/.env:9 sets `DIRECTIONAL_POSITIONAL_OPTIONS_ENABLED=true`, so the divergence is active in the running stack. No baseline item or compensating routing covers it. Live signal generation itself is unaffected (hence medium, not high) — the defect is validation-surface mismatch plus a scoring fork that diverges on any one-sided edit.

findings.title: S2-native weekly index rows are merged into S1's scan and REPLACE the monthly row even though the S2 lane is deleted — S1 enters weekly contracts
findings.summary: S2-native weekly index watchlist rows are still merged into the shared rows list that the sole remaining S1 lane scans (strategy_agent.py:2489-2507 pops the legacy monthly row and injects "NIFTY:weekly"/"NIFTY:monthly" composite rows), and _scan_entries has no expiry-track guard, so S1 evaluates and actually enters WEEKLY NIFTY/SENSEX contracts alongside monthly ones — DB shows an S1 position OPT:NIFTY:2026-07-07:23900:PE (weekly; monthly is 2026-07-28) entered/closed 2026-07-01.
findings.evidence: strategy_agent.py:683 documents S2 as 'REMOVED from _strategy_agents so no scan, no run_cycle, no positions', yet the watchlist build still calls _load_strategy2_native_watchlist_rows (strategy_agent.py:2489) which returns weekly+monthly composite rows ('NIFTY:weekly' etc., docstring at :1570-1581), then :2505 `rows_by_underlying.pop(underlying, None)` drops the S1-selected MONTHLY index row and :2506 `rows_by_underlying.update(strategy2_native_rows)` injects both tracks into the single `rows` list that S1's _scan_entries consumes. The only guard is the expiry<3-calendar-day skip.
findings.signal_impact: S1 is documented (strategy_agent.py:1-11) as the monthly physical-delivery-window MACD strategy, but for NIFTY/SENSEX it now evaluates and can enter WEEKLY ATM contracts (plus duplicate weekly+monthly rows per underlying), whose premium MACD series and theta profile differ materially from the monthly definition. Index signals recorded under the S1 lane are a blend of two contract classes, so the S1 paper test no longer measures the defined strategy on indices; a weekly-row cross can also flip-close a monthly position.
findings.fix: Since S2 is dark, stop calling _load_strategy2_native_watchlist_rows in the scan path (or filter its output to expiry_track=='monthly' before merging), keeping S1's one-monthly-row-per-underlying invariant.
findings.verifier_note: Code path verified in the working tree at /Users/ramachandran/CLAUDE PROJECTS/Nomad Curie/TradeBot/backend/paper_engine/strategy_agent.py: (a) :686-689 — S2 "REMOVED from _strategy_agents so no scan, no run_cycle, no positions"; _strategy_agents contains only _Strategy1LaneAgent. (b) :2489-2507 — `strategy2_native_rows = await self._load_strategy2_native_watchlist_rows(...)`, then `rows_by_underlying.pop(underlying, None)` and `rows_by_underlying.update(strategy2_native_rows)`; docstring at :1570-1581 confirms it returns weekly+monthly composite rows keyed "NIFTY:weekly"/"NIFTY:monthly" with the comment "so the S2 lane doesn't see the same underlying twice" — but there is no S2 lane; the merged `rows` go straight to `lane.run_cycle(rows, ...)` for S1 only. (c) StrategyEntryMixin._scan_entries (strategy_agent_entries.py:457-585) filters only on EXCLUDED_UNDERLYINGS, monthly window presence, index T-0, and `(opt_expiry - today).days < 3` — no expiry_track/weekly guard, so early-week weekly rows pass. Empirical clincher from read-only DB: agent_signals for strategy_key='macd_strategy' shows NIFTY expiry 2026-07-07 (weekly; NIFTY monthly is 2026-07-28) with 12 signal rows 06-29..07-04 including status='closed' symbol OPT:NIFTY:2026-07-07:23900:PE entered_at 2026-07-01 / closed_at 2026-07-01 — S1 actually traded a weekly contract, and both weekly (07-07) and monthly (07-28) NIFTY tracks were live under S1 simultaneously. Not covered by any baseline item (S2 deletion note documents the opposite intent; S1 uncap #2 is unrelated). Minor correction to the finder: the popped monthly row is re-supplied by the "NIFTY:monthly" composite row, so monthly coverage isn't lost — the defect is the ADDED weekly track (plus duplicate per-underlying rows), which blends two contract classes into the S1 paper-test signal stream, contradicting the module's documented monthly physical-delivery-window definition (strategy_agent.py:1-11). Severity medium: signal-generation fidelity of the S1 index lane is compromised, but stock rows and the monthly track are unaffected.

findings.title: Directional execution-ready gate force-overridden by option snapshot rows with NO recency bound — entries fire on arbitrarily stale watchlist data
findings.summary: directional_options/service.py:579-591 force-flips execution_ready=True and clears degraded_reason whenever list_live_contract_snapshots returns any rows, with no recency bound on those rows (data.py query bounds only `time <= :as_of` and `expiry >= CURRENT_DATE`), so during market hours a lagging market-intelligence refresh lets paper entries be selected and priced off arbitrarily stale watchlist LTP/IV/OI despite the stale_watchlist_seconds=600 gate having tripped.
findings.evidence: service.py:579-591: `if snapshot_rows and not bool(data_status.get("execution_ready")): ... data_status.update({... "execution_ready": True, "degraded_reason": None})` — row PRESENCE alone un-degrades the desk. The feeding query (data.py:205-215) bounds only `time <= :as_of` with `DISTINCT ON ... ORDER BY ... time DESC` and no lower bound, so day-old atm_option_watchlist_snapshots rows qualify. This defeats the stale_watchlist_seconds=600 gate computed just above and contradicts the measurement-integrity mark-freshness layer.
findings.signal_impact: On any morning where the market-intelligence watchlist refresh lags (the exact 06-29 failure mode), directional entries are selected, priced, and Greek-scored off yesterday's LTP/IV/OI rows presented as 'ready' — generating signals and paper fills at prices that never existed at signal time, which contaminates the R-multiples fed back into the RL policy posterior.
findings.fix: Require the force-override to also check row age: compute max(time) of snapshot_rows and only set execution_ready=True when as_of - max_time <= stale_watchlist_seconds; otherwise keep degraded_reason and decline entries.
findings.verifier_note: Verified end-to-end in the working tree (TradeBot/backend/directional_options/). (1) Code: service.py:579-591 reads `if snapshot_rows and not bool(data_status.get("execution_ready")): ... data_status.update({..., "execution_ready": True, "degraded_reason": None})` — row PRESENCE alone un-degrades, and it clears ANY degraded_reason (local_watchlist_stale, shared_spot_store_stale, market_intelligence_not_ready alike). (2) Query: data.py list_live_contract_snapshots has only `AND time <= :as_of` plus `expiry >= CURRENT_DATE` — no lower time bound, so prior-day rows for unexpired contracts qualify (DISTINCT ON ... ORDER BY time DESC). (3) Downstream: paper.py:256-257 `actionable = bool(signal and contract and risk.get("approved") and execution_ready)` and line 343 gates NEW entries solely on this execution_ready; entry_premium = contract option_price scored from the (possibly stale) snapshot ltp — so stale rows become paper fills at prices that never existed, feeding R-multiples to the RL policy. (4) No compensating gate: the 06-30 is_stale gate (baseline 3) applies only to the positional positioning_feed (signals.py:58), not watchlist snapshot age; selector.py has no age filter; no mark-freshness check on entry. The staleness bypass that IS deliberate (`using_latest_session` readiness_mode in _build_live_data_status) is separate — the 579 override fires precisely when that legit path did NOT apply. (5) Provenance: introduced by commit dc005669 (2026-05-08, "Reduce cloud app bootstrap latency and stale data blocking") — deliberate then, but it predates and now contradicts the 06-27/06-30 measurement-integrity + stale-gate design; no baseline item covers it. (6) Empirical: live DB shows 1217 qualifying NIFTY CE rows with latest age 2h26m ≫ 600s stale limit — the rows-present-but-stale state the override would silently un-degrade. Severity stays medium: paper-only, requires a live signal to coincide with a watchlist lag, but it directly corrupts signal-time pricing and the policy posterior on exactly the historical failure mode (06-29 market_intelligence lag).

findings.title: Directional positional 'mandatory' vol gate is a silent no-op when d_atm_iv is null — the claimed upstream enforcement does not exist
findings.summary: The positional lane's "mandatory" vol gate passes whenever d_atm_iv is null (signals.py:73 `vol_ok = (daiv is None) or ...`), the claimed upstream enforcement does not exist anywhere, and d_atm_iv is NULL on 100% of positioning rows since 2026-06-25 — so the gate is currently a total no-op, inverting the researched definition (backtest_indices_monthly.py:111 treats NaN as gate-FAIL and skips the trade).
findings.evidence: signals.py:73 `vol_ok = (daiv is None) or (float(daiv) >= 0.0)  # live vol gate enforced upstream when history IV is null` — grep of service.py/positioning_feed.py shows no d_atm_iv/vol-gate enforcement anywhere upstream. positioning_feed.py:4-5 documents d_atm_iv as "the mandatory long-premium vol gate", and it is null whenever atm_iv is missing for a session (greeks coverage is partial: NIFTY 393/428 sessions, BANKNIFTY 265/312 per the positioning panel build) and always on the first panel row.
findings.signal_impact: The vol-state research (IV-percentile gate, fwd straddle IC -0.305) made the vol gate a mandatory component of the positional entry; on sessions with missing IV history the lane silently takes long-premium entries the strategy definition forbids, so the paper record mixes gated and ungated entries and cannot cleanly measure the researched positioning-confirmation edge.
findings.fix: Fail closed: treat daiv None as vol_ok=False (decline entry) or implement the referenced upstream live-IV check (compare current chain ATM IV vs prior session) before allowing None to pass; log which branch fired into the journal for attribution.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in working tree (TradeBot/backend/directional_options/). (1) signals.py:73 reads exactly `vol_ok = (daiv is None) or (float(daiv) >= 0.0)  # live vol gate enforced upstream when history IV is null` — None → vol_ok=True. (2) The comment's claim is false: positioning_feed.latest() (lines 181-199) just returns the raw row (`"d_atm_iv": row.d_atm_iv`) with is_stale; service.py:508-518 passes it straight to predict() with no vol/d_atm_iv check; grep of service.py/paper.py finds zero other d_atm_iv/vol-gate references. (3) The researched strategy treats missing IV as BLOCKING: backtest_indices_monthly.py:110-111 `div = d_atm_iv.get(day, np.nan); if pd.isna(div) or div < 0:   # mandatory vol gate` → skip. Live does the opposite. (4) DB evidence (read-only): directional_positioning_daily has null d_atm_iv on 9/134 BANKNIFTY, 9/125 NIFTY/SENSEX rows historically, but every row from 2026-06-25 through latest (2026-07-03) has atm_iv and d_atm_iv NULL for ALL underlyings — the gate has been silently disabled on every recent session, so any positional entry since then was taken ungated. Not covered by baseline item 3 (that fix was stops/DTE/is_stale, not the vol gate) and is_stale does not compensate (recent rows are fresh, just IV-less). Severity stays medium: paper-mode lane, side/confirm logic still applies, but the IV-gate research (straddle IC −0.305) is unenforced and the paper record mixes gated/ungated entries — plus the upstream atm_iv pipeline going all-NULL since 06-25 deserves its own fix.

findings.title: S1 has NO expiry/window-end exit — positions can ride into the physical-delivery window and expiry on stale marks
findings.summary: S1's exit cascade has no expiry/window-end/DTE exit (window_end deliberately deleted 2026-06-02 as "over-firing", leaving only hard_stop/target/macd_reversal), asymmetric with entries' T-0 and 3-day-expiry skips — and DB evidence shows 8 of 45 closed macd_strategy positions were only closed INSIDE the physical-delivery window (expiry-7..expiry); however the "marks freeze so exits NEVER fire / zombies ride through expiry" escalation is overstated: 0 positions have ever remained open past expiry, and the only past-expiry open row is unit-test residue.
findings.evidence: exits.py:9-29 documents the trimmed cascade: '#2 window_end (premature expiry-fade close)' is DELETED, leaving only -25% hard stop, +50% partial, display-only trail, and macd_reversal_30m. Grep of exits.py shows no dte/expiry-based close (expiry appears only in mark queries). Yet the module docstring (strategy_agent.py:5) defines the lane as 'Physical-delivery trading window (prev_expiry-7 to current_expiry-7)' and entries enforce a T-0 index skip and a 3-day expiry skip — asymmetric: entries respect the window, exits do not.
findings.signal_impact: A monthly stock-option position held past window end leaves the ATM watchlist, so its snapshot/candle marks freeze; the -25% stop and macd_reversal exits then evaluate against frozen premiums and may NEVER fire, leaving zombie positions through the delivery window into expiry. Those unbounded holds pollute open-position counts, equity, and the per-signal outcome record of the uncapped signal-generation test (MACD_STRATEGY_MAX_POSITIONS=1000 amplifies how many such zombies can accumulate).
findings.fix: Add a forced close (reason='window_end') when today >= expiry - 7d (matching the entry-window math from window_calculator), or at minimum an expiry-1d hard exit at last known mark, independent of MACD state.
findings.verifier_note: Code check (working tree, TradeBot/backend/paper_engine/strategy_agent_exits.py): the cascade comment at lines 22-24 confirms "#2 window_end (premature expiry-fade close)" is deleted; the loop body (lines 154-209) contains only hard_stop, target_50pct, display-only trail, and macd_reversal_30m — no dte/expiry test anywhere (expiry appears only in mark queries). Entries side confirmed asymmetric: strategy_agent_entries.py:559-576 enforces T-0 skip ("expiry_day_skip_t0") and a hard `(opt_expiry - today).days < 3` skip ("expiry_within_3_days"). No compensating expiry sweep exists for S1 — only commodity_strategy_agent.py:3026 has an "expired_contract" close; the DB restore path (_restore_strategy1_positions_from_db, strategy_agent.py:1703+) also restores without any expiry filter. Empirical: `SELECT ... FROM agent_positions WHERE strategy_key='macd_strategy' AND status='closed'` → 8/45 closed with updated_at inside (expiry-7, expiry], i.e. positions demonstrably ride past window end into the delivery window; 26 currently-open positions are all 2026-07-28 expiry (window ends ~Jul 21, so pre-window today). REFUTED sub-claims: (a) closed_after_expiry = 0 — no position has ever zombied through expiry; exits did fire inside the window, because (b) the mark-freeze mechanism is weaker than claimed: _manage_exits calls load_candles with allow_broker_refresh enabled unless PAPER_TRADING_ONLY/MARKET_INTELLIGENCE_STRATEGY_LOCAL_ONLY (neither set in container printenv; both default False in core/config.py:147,161), so the TTL-bounded gap-aware backfill (baseline #4) keeps marking off-watchlist contracts while they still trade. (c) The one open past-expiry row (strategy1 / SENSEX 2026-05-29 75000 CE, entered_at 2026-07-05, current_price==entry_price) exactly matches the fixture in tests/test_paper_strategy_agent.py:666-682 ("strategy1"/"Strategy 1", SENSEX 2026-05-29, SENSEX75000CE) — unit-test residue written to the production DB, not a live zombie (itself a separate hygiene issue). Not covered by any baseline item (baseline #3 stop/target/DTE-exit fix was the directional lane, not S1). Net: real, deliberate-deletion-turned-gap that measurably lets ~18% of S1 outcomes be decided in the delivery-window regime the strategy doc excludes — medium for signal-generation fidelity, but the unbounded-zombie amplification does not hold.

findings.title: S1 signal-flip closes the existing position BEFORE downstream gates and even while the kill switch is active — a blocked flip leaves the book flat
findings.summary: S1 signal-flip closes the existing opposite-side position before the new entry passes downstream gates (missing-LTP, IV sanity, dedupe, MP gate, learning gate, capacity) and before the kill-switch check at :986, so a gated flip leaves the book flat with a misleading signal_flip_to_* close record, and flip closes still execute while set_kill_switch is active.
findings.evidence: entries.py:786-811: on an opposite-side signal, `await self._close_position(runtime, existing, exit_ltp, f"signal_flip_to_{opt_type}")` runs immediately, while the new entry must still pass missing-LTP (:817), IV scaler (:848), already_processed (:860), MP gate (:866), learning gate, and the kill switch — which is checked only at :986 (`if self._kill_switch_active: ... new entries are blocked`) AFTER candidates are assembled. The design comment (:781-783) states the strategy 'stays in the market but on the side the new tape wants'.
findings.signal_impact: Whenever a flip signal is subsequently blocked (stale data, IV>90%, dedupe, learning gate, kill switch), the recorded outcome is a naked close — the book goes flat where the strategy definition says it should be positioned the other way; with the kill switch active the lane still exits positions on flip signals it is forbidden to act on. Flip-labelled closes in the signal record therefore do not correspond to actual flips, skewing per-reason outcome attribution.
findings.fix: Evaluate all entry gates (including kill switch) for the new side FIRST and only close the existing leg when the replacement entry is approved; otherwise persist a 'flip_blocked' observation and keep the position.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in working tree at TradeBot/backend/paper_engine/strategy_agent_entries.py. The close runs at :790-800 ("await self._close_position(runtime, existing, exit_ltp, f\"signal_flip_to_{opt_type}\")") followed by gates that `continue` without re-entry: missing_ltp, "if iv_scaler <= 0", already_processed, and "if not mp_gate.get(\"confirmed\")". The only kill-switch check in the file is :986 ("if self._kill_switch_active: ... new entries are blocked ... return"), after candidate assembly. Traced the call chain: _loop → run_once (strategy_agent.py:2203) → lane _scan_entries (:573) has no earlier kill-switch gate on the S1 path; set_kill_switch (:4823) sets the flag without cancelling the loop task or flattening positions (only engage_manual_kill_switch flattens), so flip closes do fire under an active kill switch. Design comment :778-782 explicitly states the strategy "stays in the market but on the side the new tape wants" — violated whenever the replacement entry is gated. Minor correction to the finder's evidence: the data_stale quality block (:762-769) precedes the close, so stale data does NOT cause naked closes; all other cited gates do. No baseline item covers this (baseline #3 is the directional lane, not S1 MACD). Severity medium: skews flip/close attribution in the signal record and breaks kill-switch semantics, but entry-signal generation itself is unaffected.

findings.title: Per-cycle why-no-trade and signal-coverage telemetry is ephemeral — logs and in-memory dicts only, no queryable history
findings.summary: Per-cycle coverage and why-no-trade attribution is not persisted anywhere queryable: auction's no_trade_gate/flat_reasons/gate_breakdown reach only logger.info and the in-memory last_result_meta, S1's scanned_rows is dropped even from the live status payload, and the one persisted sink (_emit_scan_audit -> agent_audit_events) records "scanned 0 symbol(s)" with empty per_symbol for market_intelligence successes — so a coverage collapse that doesn't hard-fail (the normal partial-coverage mode under the time-budget/round-robin fix) leaves no after-the-fact evidence; only hard failures (scan_cycle_failed) persist.
findings.evidence: Auction's why-no-trade gate attribution goes only to `logger.info("auction.cycle symbol={sym} gate={gate} ...")` (line 257) and the returned dict (no_trade_gate/flat_reasons, lines 271-274) whose sole consumer is the supervisor's in-memory last_result_meta — grep shows no other consumer of `no_trade_gate`. S1's coverage counter is reset every cycle (`self.runtime.last_run_summary = {"counters": {}, ..., "scanned_rows": len(rows)}`, strategy_agent.py:565-570) and the status payload (strategy_agent.py:503-509) exposes only counters/blocked_reasons — `scanned_rows` is dropped even from the live status. macd_refined's stage funnel (live.py:337-339) lives only in the returned status dict. _emit_scan_audit dedupes to fingerprint-change/30-min heartbeat and captures only the first 8 per_symbol summaries.
findings.signal_impact: There is no persisted time series of "of N eligible instruments, M were actually evaluated / blocked by gate X" for any lane. The 06-29 starvation (scan saw ~14-16 of 217 names for days) is exactly the class of regression this hides: coverage collapse is invisible after the fact because the evidence lives in rotated docker logs and memory wiped by restart. Signal absence cannot be distinguished between 'strategy correctly declined' and 'instrument never evaluated'.
findings.fix: Persist a compact per-cycle coverage row (lane, ts, universe_size, evaluated, per-gate block counts, no_trade_gate) — agent_audit_events already exists as a sink (S1's _tally shows the pattern); include scanned_rows in the S1 status payload; graph coverage on the ops dashboard so starvation is visible same-day.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in working tree + production DB. (1) backend/auction_intelligence/automation.py: gate computed lines 245-274, logged line 257; sole consumer of no_trade_gate is the in-memory rollup at line 315 ("gate_breakdown[gate] = ...") returned into runtime.last_result_meta (RunnerRuntime field, memory only). (2) _emit_scan_audit (market_hours_paper_supervisor.py:889-998) DOES persist to agent_audit_events — a real INSERT via record_audit_event (agentic_rag/audit_agent.py:33) — so "no queryable history" is mildly overstated for failures: DB has 170 market_intelligence scan_cycle_failed rows covering the 06-29 starvation era.
