findings.title: S1's relative-IV sizing policy is dead: market_iv_pct is read from a dict keyed by instrument_key, so it is always None and the scaler silently compares against a hardcoded 22% constant
findings.summary: S1's relative-IV sizing is dead code: market_iv_pct is looked up on snapshot_state (a dict keyed instrument_key -> {rank: row}, with no market-IV producer anywhere in the backend), so it is always None and every signal's iv_size_scaler and iv_status bucket are computed against the hardcoded 22% fallback instead of actual market IV — distorting position sizing and the journaled iv_status/iv_size_note attribution, though it never blocks or creates signals (only the IV>=90% sanity reject can block).
findings.evidence: entries.py:842-846: market_iv_pct = float(snapshot_state.get("market_iv_pct") or snapshot_state.get("market_iv") or 0.0) or None — but _load_strategy1_recent_snapshot_state (entries.py:91-206) returns a dict mapping instrument_key -> {rank: row} and never sets a 'market_iv_pct' key, so both lookups are always None. agent/iv_size_policy.py:59-63 then falls back: 'if market_iv_pct is None: market_iv_pct = 22.0  # median NSE F&O IV historical average'.
findings.signal_impact: The documented relative-IV policy ('40% IV when market IV is 38% is just average') is silently absolute: in a market-wide vol spike every instrument reads as 'iv_spread_extreme' and gets quartered to 0.25x size, and in a vol crush overpriced contracts get full size — plus the iv_status preferred/acceptable/cautious tags journaled with every S1 signal (and consumed by strategy_learning) are systematically mislabeled, corrupting the per-signal attribution the paper test is meant to produce.
findings.fix: Compute an actual market IV reference per cycle (e.g. median watchlist ATM IV across the scanned rows, or index ATM IV) and pass it explicitly into the entry scan instead of reading it from snapshot_state.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in working tree. (1) strategy_agent_entries.py:842-846 reads `snapshot_state.get("market_iv_pct") or snapshot_state.get("market_iv")`; but `_load_strategy1_recent_snapshot_state` (lines 91-206) returns `state.setdefault(instrument_key, {})[rank] = dict(row)` — keys are instrument_keys only, so both lookups always miss and `float(None or None or 0.0) or None` → None. (2) Repo-wide grep for "market_iv" shows NO producer anywhere in backend/ — the only writers are the dead reads themselves, so agent/iv_size_policy.py:58-62 `if market_iv_pct is None: market_iv_pct = 22.0` is the only path ever taken, despite the module docstring declaring "The correct quantity is the *spread vs market IV*, not the absolute level" — this contradicts, not confirms, deliberateness. (3) Downstream impact confirmed: line 1090 `fraction *= max(0.25, min(1.0, iv_size_scaler_value))` scales lot sizing, and iv_status (lines 854-858) feeds sizing_mode at line 1245-1249 ("preferred"→premium Kelly fraction) plus journaled tags. Not covered by any baseline item. Corrections to finder's claims: (a) strategy_learning.py keys scores off strategy_key/underlying/option_type/signal_reason only — it does NOT consume iv_status, so the "corrupting strategy_learning attribution" claim is overstated; (b) signals are never blocked by this (scaler floor is 0.25; 0.0 only on IV>=90 sanity), so impact is sizing/labeling fidelity, not signal existence. DB check: only 1 strategy1 agent_signal in last 7 days, metadata lacks iv keys (no journaled counter-evidence either way). Severity medium stands: a documented sizing policy is 100% inoperative in the exact regime (market-wide vol shifts) it was built for, and mislabels every journaled S1 signal's iv_status.

findings.title: CBE pass-2 'unclassified' F&O names are structurally untradeable (bias can never confirm), silently shrinking the scanned universe by ~8% despite the comment claiming they remain tradeable
findings.summary: CBE pass-2 candidates are tagged stock_quadrant="unclassified" (alpha_engine.py:302), but _bias_from_signals only emits a non-neutral bias when the quadrant is in {leading, improving} or {lagging, weakening}, and paper.py:295-296 skips any row whose bias is not bullish/bearish — so the 17 unclassified F&O names (~8% of the universe) are fetched and scored every cycle yet can never generate a CBE signal, contradicting the pass-2 comment "still tradeable".
findings.evidence: alpha_engine.py:291 comment: '# Pass 2 — F&O symbols missing from any sector slice still tradeable.' then :302 sets "stock_quadrant": "unclassified". But _bias_from_signals (:757-759) requires stock_q in {leading, improving} or {lagging, weakening} for any non-neutral bias — 'unclassified' can never pass. DB, latest cbe_scan_run: stock_quadrant='unclassified' count=17, non_neutral bias=0 (vs leading 46/23 non-neutral, lagging 75/18).
findings.signal_impact: 17 of ~215 F&O names are fetched, indicator-scored and ranked every hourly cycle yet can never emit a CBE long/short signal — a silent, permanent coverage hole in the lane's signal universe (dead compute plus no visibility that these names are excluded), which directly contradicts the paper-mode objective of measuring signal generation across the defined universe.
findings.fix: Either let unclassified names pass the RRG leg (treat quadrant as neutral-permissive with a score haircut) to match the comment, or exclude them before indicator scoring and surface an 'unclassified_excluded' count in the scan-run telemetry.
findings.verifier_note: Verified all three legs myself in the working tree at TradeBot/backend/cbe_scanner/. (1) alpha_engine.py pass-2 loop: comment "# Pass 2 — F&O symbols missing from any sector slice still tradeable." then sets `"stock_quadrant": "unclassified"` (line 302). (2) _bias_from_signals: `rrg_bull = stock_q in {"leading", "improving"}`; `rrg_bear = stock_q in {"lagging", "weakening"}`; both bullish and bearish branches require rrg_bull/rrg_bear, so "unclassified" always falls through to `return "neutral"`. No remapping of unclassified elsewhere (grep: only occurrence in cbe_scanner is line 302; paper.py "unclassified" hits are sector_code defaults, unrelated). (3) paper.py entry gate: `if bias not in ("bullish", "bearish"): continue` — neutral never trades. DB re-run confirms finder's numbers exactly: latest run has unclassified n=17, non_neutral=0 (vs leading 46/23, lagging 75/18); across ALL historical runs 1187 unclassified rows, 17 distinct names, ZERO ever non-neutral. Not covered by any baseline item (baseline CBE item is the v4 direction-aware review; this exclusion is not listed as deliberate). Severity medium is right: permanent silent exclusion of ~8% of the paper-mode signal universe plus dead per-cycle compute, but the other ~92% of names are unaffected.

findings.title: FMP order-flow confirmation runs on fabricated inputs: CRUDEOIL is keyed to a hardcoded expired future with zero market_ticks rows, and index quote history carries no real bid/ask, yet signal confidence is adjusted by 'order-flow alignment'
findings.summary: FMP's order-flow confirmation adjusts signal confidence (+0.08/-0.05 around the 0.55 actionability threshold) and selects balance-extreme setups from largely synthetic inputs: index ticks carry no book (0 of 206k NIFTY50-INDEX rows in 5 days have bid>0) so bid/ask are fabricated as LTP±tick with size 1.0 yet labeled source="market_ticks"/tick_ready=true, and CRUDEOIL is pinned to the expired hardcoded MCX:CRUDEOIL26JUNFUT (0 market_ticks rows ever) so it permanently runs on bar-inferred proxy flow.
findings.evidence: service.py:1781: app_symbol = INDEX_APP_SYMBOLS[symbol_code] where config.py:24 pins "CRUDEOIL": "MCX:CRUDEOIL26JUNFUT" (expired June-2026 future; month-coded literal). DB: market_ticks has ZERO rows for any %CRUDEOIL% symbol, so _recent_quote_history is always empty → _build_bar_order_flow fallback. For indices the rows exist but carry no book: NIFTY50-INDEX last 3 days = 6347 tick rows, 0 with bid>0 or bid_qty>0, and service.py:2003-2005 then fabricates 'bid = round(ltp - tick_size, 2); ask = round(ltp + tick_size, 2)'. _build_signal still applies order_flow_alignment to confidence and gates balance-extreme setups on this synthetic order flow.
findings.signal_impact: FMP's setup confidence (0.55 actionability threshold) is nudged up/down by an 'order-flow' signal that is either bar-inferred or synthesized from LTP±tick with zero sizes — so paper signals fire or get suppressed on noise dressed as confirmation, and the CRUDEOIL leg additionally depends on a config literal that silently rots every contract month.
findings.fix: Derive the CRUDEOIL order-flow symbol from resolve_upstox_mcx_future (same roll logic as position mapping) instead of the static literal; when quote history has no genuine sized quotes, tag order_flow as 'synthetic' and zero its confidence contribution instead of applying alignment adjustments.
findings.verifier_note: Verified every empirical claim myself. config.py:24 = "CRUDEOIL": "MCX:CRUDEOIL26JUNFUT" (expired). DB: market_ticks %CRUDEOIL% count = 0; NSE:NIFTY50-INDEX last 5d = 206,336 rows, 0 with bid>0 or bid_qty>0 (SENSEX 68,581/0). service.py:2003-2006: "if bid <= 0: bid = round(ltp - tick_size, 2)" (ask likewise), sizes floored to 1.0; line 1838 labels it source="market_ticks" and line 1926 "tick_ready = order_flow_source == \"market_ticks\"" so the readiness gate treats the fabricated book as real. _build_signal lines 1637-1643 gate daily_balance_extreme_reversion setups on order_flow_direction (delta sign) and 1684-1689 apply confidence +=0.08/-=0.05. Mitigations found: tick-rule aggressor inference from LTP sequence retains some real signal, and for MCX the bar-proxy is a semi-deliberate accepted mode (futures_proxy_ready, line 1927) — but the expired contract literal makes real CRUDEOIL tick flow permanently unreachable and no baseline item covers the FMP lane (item 9's kill-switch layer is the auction lane). Severity stays medium per finder: real confidence-threshold impact on paper signal generation, not a P/L-only nit.

findings.title: S1 exit marks have no recency bound or staleness gate — once a contract leaves the ATM watchlist, stop/reversal exits go blind on a frozen price
findings.summary: S1's exit cascade has no mark-staleness gate and no DTE/expiry exit, so exits silently run on a frozen price if the per-position broker refresh fails or the contract passes expiry — but the finder's headline mechanism is wrong: leaving the ATM watchlist does NOT freeze the mark, because _manage_exits itself broker-refreshes each held contract's candles every cycle.
findings.evidence: _latest_position_quote_map (exits.py:282-341) selects `ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1` over a UNION of atm_option_watchlist_snapshots and option_premium_candles with NO lower time bound; the observed timestamp is stored into `pos.price_updated_at` (exits.py:121) but nothing in the exit cascade checks it — no staleness comparison exists anywhere in the file (grep for 'stale' only matches nothing in exit logic).
findings.signal_impact: S1's only exits are the -25% hard stop and the 30m MACD zero-down reversal, both computed off this mark. When a position's contract drops off the ATM watchlist (spot drifts, expiry rolls) its snapshots and candles stop updating; the mark freezes at the last row, ret pins near its last value, and neither exit can ever fire — the position is a zombie whose exit signals are never generated. With no DTE/window-end exit in the cascade this persists to expiry, so paper-mode exit-signal correctness (and every downstream learning score fed from these trades) is corrupted.
findings.fix: Add a recency bound (e.g. time >= now - interval '2 days') plus an explicit staleness branch: if the freshest mark is older than N minutes during RTH, trigger a broker refresh via option_history_service.load_candles(allow_broker_refresh=True) or force a管理 exit path (stale_mark_exit), and emit an audit event instead of silently holding.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in TradeBot/backend/paper_engine/strategy_agent_exits.py: (a) _latest_position_quote_map (lines 282-344) is indeed `ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1` over the snapshots∪candles UNION with no lower time bound; (b) `pos.price_updated_at` (line 121) is only used to prevent regressing to OLDER marks (lines 241-243, 377-378) — no staleness check exists anywhere in the exit cascade; (c) the cascade is only hard_stop/-25%, target_50pct, trail-for-display, and macd_reversal_30m — the header comment (lines 22-29) shows window_end was deliberately deleted, and no expiry-settlement logic exists anywhere in paper_engine/. HOWEVER the claimed failure trigger is neutralized by compensating logic the finder missed: _manage_exits line 75-84 calls option_history_service.load_candles per position with allow_broker_refresh=not(MARKET_INTELLIGENCE_STRATEGY_LOCAL_ONLY or PAPER_TRADING_ONLY) — both default False in core/config.py (lines 147, 161) and neither is set in TradeBot/.env or docker-compose.yml, so refresh is ON. In market_data/option_history.py lines 638-660, `_latest_row_is_stale_for_today` (line 170: latest bar from a previous day, or intraday older than one bar+buffer) triggers a broker fetch keyed by pos.instrument_key (set at entry, strategy_agent_entries.py:1055/1131) and `_persist_broker_candles` writes rows back into option_premium_candles — which the quote-map UNION reads. So an off-ATM-watchlist contract keeps getting fresh marks every 60s cycle until expiry; the "zombie the moment spot drifts" scenario does not occur in the deployed config. What survives is a narrower real defect: with no staleness comparison and no expiry exit, a silent broker-refresh failure (auth expiry, API outage — no kill-switch on this lane, unlike the directional lane's mark-freshness gate in baseline item 9) or a position still open at expiry (broker returns no new bars, MACD frozen, ret pinned) leaves a permanently unclosable position whose exit signal is never generated and never scored. Could not confirm empirically whether any such zombie exists in the positions table — Docker daemon hung on every psql attempt (docker exec/docker ps all timed out), so the DB check was unavailable. Severity corrected high→low: the systematic "every off-watchlist position goes blind" impact is refuted; the residual is a conditional edge (refresh-failure window or held-to-expiry pin) on a paper lane, though adding a staleness kill-switch + expiry settlement to S1 (mirroring the directional lane) is a legitimate follow-up.

findings.title: Auction lane computes the full 'analyze' pipeline twice per symbol per 180s cycle
findings.summary: The auction paper cycle does run the full analyze_with_options pipeline twice per symbol per 180s cycle (live.py:472 for the shadow snapshot, service.py:208 via automation.py:210 for the paper book), but the first bundle is not discarded (it feeds shadow records with honest live gates while the second run uses paper-override inputs), the measured whole-cycle cost is ~90s — well under the 300s timeout — and the compute is thread-offloaded, so this is a real ~2x CPU inefficiency with no demonstrated timeout, dropped-signal, or 60s-lane-stall impact.
findings.evidence: capture_live_paper_cycle first runs `snapshot = await build_live_analysis(symbol_code=symbol)` (line 177) — which internally executes `bundle = await service.analyze_with_options(...)` (live.py:472) — then discards that bundle, re-instantiates `service = AuctionIntelligenceService(paper_mode=True)` and re-runs `service.analyze_and_record_option_paper(...)` (lines 209-219) on the same request bars/quote/trades, which calls analyze_with_options again (service.py:208). service.py:172 documents analyze() as a '200-320s compute' CPU block.
findings.signal_impact: The dominant CPU cost of the auction MP+OF lane runs 2x per symbol (NIFTY+BANKNIFTY serially, run_market_hours_cycle line 295-299) inside a 300s runner timeout on a 180s interval — cycles that overrun are killed by the supervisor and the paper book never syncs that cycle, so auction signals are silently dropped or delayed; the wasted CPU also inflates the awaited supervisor batch, stalling the 60s lanes (finding 1).
findings.fix: Reuse the AnalysisBundle already produced inside build_live_analysis: return the bundle (or accept paper-mode session/portfolio overrides in build_live_analysis) and feed it straight to paper.record_analysis/sync_positions instead of re-running MarketProfile/OrderFlow/Regime/agents on identical bars; only the risk-governor stage needs re-evaluation with the paper overrides.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in working tree: automation.py:177 "snapshot = await build_live_analysis(symbol_code=symbol)" → live.py:471-472 "service = AuctionIntelligenceService(); bundle = await service.analyze_with_options(...)"; then automation.py:209-210 "service = AuctionIntelligenceService(paper_mode=True); bundle, ... = await service.analyze_and_record_option_paper(...)" → service.py:208 calls analyze_with_options again. So the double compute exists. Three claims are overstated: (1) "discards that bundle" is wrong — automation.py:220 builds shadow records from snapshot["analysis"], and the second run intentionally differs (paper overrides broker_connected/stale_data_seconds/net_liquidation, lines 179-208 comments), so the runs have different gate semantics; (2) the "200-320s compute" figure is not auction analyze() — commit 8f3e243a shows it refers to the five heavy lanes collectively (the ~300s one was the CBE universe screen), and analyze() is offloaded via asyncio.to_thread (service.py:174), so it cannot stall the 60s lanes' event loop; (3) the timeout-kill impact is unsupported — commit aaedcc95 (which added the [AuctionProfile] per-symbol timing log) measured the entire auction cycle, double compute included, at ~90s, well inside the 300s supervisor timeout (core/config.py:156, no per-runner override at supervisor lines 554-560) and the 180s interval. Could not pull live logs/DB (Docker daemon unresponsive: docker CLI and unix-socket /_ping both hung; backend :8000 resets connections — NSE closed weekend), but the git-measured timing plus thread offload refute the high-severity signal-drop mechanism. Net: real duplicate-compute inefficiency worth fixing (share one analysis or pass the paper bundle to the shadow builder), immaterial to correct signal generation today.

findings.title: S1 rebuilds a 7-day, all-instrument 15m MACD from raw snapshot rows every 60s scan with no cache
findings.summary: S1's 15m re-entry path recomputes a 7-day, all-instrument MACD from raw atm_option_watchlist_snapshots rows on every 60s scan with no caching — real wasted DB/CPU work per cycle, but the query is index-backed and only adds seconds at most, so it does not meaningfully delay 15m/30m cross evaluation.
findings.evidence: _scan_entries (called every 60s cycle) does `macd15 = await self._load_strategy1_15m_macd_from_snapshots(rows)` (line 488) which runs `SELECT instrument_key, time, ltp FROM atm_option_watchlist_snapshots WHERE instrument_key = ANY(:instrument_keys) AND ... time > now() - make_interval(days => :lookback_days)` with lookback_days=7 for EVERY CE/PE instrument in the ~217-name watchlist (lines 244-258), then re-buckets and recomputes MACD(12,26,9) per contract in Python (lines 286-297). No memoization; only the last two 15m bars are ever consumed (lines 292-295).
findings.signal_impact: Tens of thousands of rows (measured ~68k rows/7d) are refetched and resampled every minute inside S1's own untimed loop (asyncio.sleep(60) runs AFTER completion) — a slow rebuild directly stretches the effective scan interval, so fresh 30m zero-crosses and 15m re-entry crosses are evaluated late and entries land bars after the signal. The per-minute hypertable scan also competes with every other lane's DB reads.
findings.fix: Cache the per-instrument 15m bucket series in memory keyed by instrument_key and only fetch rows newer than the last cached snapshot time each cycle (incremental append), or precompute/persist the 15m MACD inside the ATM watchlist snapshot writer the way the 30m MACD already is.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in working tree: strategy_agent_entries.py:488 `macd15 = await self._load_strategy1_15m_macd_from_snapshots(rows)` inside `_scan_entries`, gated only by `NSE_S1_ALLOW_15M_REENTRY: bool = True` (core/config.py:179, no .env override); the loader (lines 208-308) runs `SELECT instrument_key, time, ltp ... time > now() - make_interval(days => :lookback_days)` with lookback_days=7 for all CE/PE keys, re-buckets and runs compute_macd per contract, and uses only `macd_line[-1]/[-2]`; grep confirms no memoization. Loop cadence confirmed: strategy_agent.py:660 `scan_interval_seconds = 60` and :1050 `await asyncio.sleep(self.scan_interval_seconds)` after run_once completes. However, severity is overstated: migration 005 shows `idx_atm_watchlist_snapshots_instrument (instrument_key, time DESC)` on a 1-day-chunk hypertable, so the ~68k-row fetch (finder's own number; I could not re-run it — Docker daemon/DB container were unresponsive during verification: docker ps timed out, port 5433 closed) plus Python bucketing costs seconds at most; the primary 30m signal path uses a separate single-day query; a few seconds of loop stretch cannot make 15m/30m bar signals land 'bars late'. Not covered by baseline item 1 (that fix is the market_intelligence runner, a different loop). Legit fix: cache buckets per instrument and append only new snapshots, or shrink lookback to the ~36-bar MACD warm-up (~1.5 sessions).

findings.title: S1 exit loop is N+1 per open position: an unbounded two-hypertable UNION query plus a broker-refresh-capable load_candles per position per 60s cycle
findings.summary: The S1 exit loop is genuinely N+1 per open position (26 currently open on the uncapped lane): one no-time-bound UNION quote query plus one broker-refresh-capable load_candles per position per 60s cycle, sequentially before the entry scan, with the stale-today refresh trigger lacking any TTL (retries a failing contract every cycle on the shared Upstox limiter) — but the quote query is index-backed and fast (~22ms exec, not a full-history sort), the whole loop runs in the agent's own 60s task (not the market_intelligence 300s-budgeted runner), and a successful refresh keeps a 30-min-bar contract fresh for ~30min, so at current book size the impact is a few seconds of intra-cycle entry-scan delay plus mild shared-limiter contention, degrading only if the book grows large or broker fetches persistently fail.
findings.evidence: _manage_exits iterates `for symbol, pos in list(runtime.positions.items()):` calling `await option_history_service.load_candles(... allow_broker_refresh=not (...))` per position (lines 74-84), and _latest_position_quote_map loops `for pos in positions:` issuing one `UNION ALL ... ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1` query per position over atm_option_watchlist_snapshots + option_premium_candles filtered by underlying/expiry/strike/option_type with NO time lower bound and no instrument_key (lines 292-326).
findings.signal_impact: With MACD_STRATEGY_MAX_POSITIONS deliberately uncapped at 1000 for signal-generation testing, the book can hold dozens+ of positions; each 60s cycle then does N sequential full-history sorts plus up to N load_candles (each able to trigger TTL-bounded Upstox backfill on the shared UPSTOX_DATA_LIMITER that market_intelligence's premium top-up depends on). Exits run FIRST in run_once, so a slow exit pass delays the entry scan of the same cycle — late crosses and late stop/reversal exits.
findings.fix: Replace the per-position loop with one batched query (DISTINCT ON (underlying,expiry,strike,option_type) ... WHERE (underlying,expiry,strike,option_type) IN (...) AND time > now() - interval '2 days'), add a time lower bound, and gate the per-position load_candles broker refresh to positions whose 30m series is actually stale rather than every position every minute.
findings.verifier_note: Checked working-tree code + live system. Confirmed: strategy_agent_exits.py:74-84 loops positions calling load_candles with allow_broker_refresh=not(MARKET_INTELLIGENCE_STRATEGY_LOCAL_ONLY or PAPER_TRADING_ONLY) — both default False (core/config.py:147,161) and are unset in .env/container env, so broker refresh IS enabled; _latest_position_quote_map (lines 292-326) issues one per-position query with no time lower bound; exits precede entries at strategy_agent.py:571 ('await self.owner._manage_exits(self.runtime, rows)' then '_scan_entries'); the fetch path shares UPSTOX_DATA_LIMITER (option_history.py:301, 8/s + 1800/30min); the needs_live_refresh trigger at option_history.py:638/650 has no TTL (only gap-backfill has _GAP_BACKFILL_TTL_SECONDS=1800). Live DB: 26 open macd_strategy positions. Severity reduced from medium: EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the exact query = 21.7ms execution via idx_opc_contract ordered index scans with LIMIT 1 (378ms cold planning across chunks, plan-cached per connection) — the 'unbounded sort' characterization is wrong; and the loop runs in the agent's OWN 60s asyncio loop (strategy_agent.py:1040-1050, scan_interval_seconds=60), NOT inside the market_intelligence runner, so it cannot trip that runner's 300s timeout — cross-runner impact is only limiter contention, ~52 broker calls/hr steady-state for 26 positions vs a 3600/hr shared budget. No empirical slow-cycle data was obtainable (agent_risk_state retains only 07-04 onward; container restarted).

findings.title: market_intelligence runs an unbounded COUNT(DISTINCT underlying) over the full snapshots hypertable every 60s cycle
findings.summary: refresh_nse_watchlists' freshness probe runs an unbounded COUNT(DISTINCT underlying) over the whole atm_option_watchlist_snapshots hypertable (no time predicate, no retention policy) on nearly every 60s MI cycle; measured 127ms today on 109k rows and growing ~7k rows/day, but currently immaterial to the 300s budget.
findings.evidence: refresh_nse_watchlists' freshness probe (executed on every cycle where full refresh isn't already due, i.e. ~14 of every 15 cycles) runs `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT underlying) FROM atm_option_watchlist_snapshots WHERE kind = 'STOCK'` with no time predicate (lines 381-389) alongside the today-bounded count.
findings.signal_impact: The query cost grows monotonically with the hypertable (~68k rows/week and growing) and executes inside the market_intelligence runner that the supervisor deliberately awaits FIRST and serially — every millisecond it takes is inherited startup latency for directional_options, gann and auction on the same pass, and it eats into MI's 300s budget shared with the premium top-up that feeds S1 signal generation.
findings.fix: Bound the baseline to the recent past (e.g. `AND time > now() - interval '7 days'` with DISTINCT-per-latest-session, or take MAX over a per-day continuous aggregate), and/or cache stock_latest in memory for the session — it only changes when the universe changes.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in working tree: market_intelligence_runtime.py runs `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT underlying) FROM atm_option_watchlist_snapshots WHERE kind = 'STOCK'` (no time bound) alongside the today-bounded count whenever full_refresh_due is false — the comment says it wants the "last-session count", so it's also semantically wider than intended. Re-ran the query with EXPLAIN ANALYZE on prod DB: seq-scans all 16 chunks, 108,906 rows total, execution time 126.9ms. timescaledb_information.jobs shows NO retention/compression policy on the table, so cost grows linearly (~7k rows/day → roughly seconds-scale in a year). Not covered by baseline item 1 (that fixed the premium top-up, not this probe) and no compensating gate. Downgraded to low: 0.13s of a 300s budget has no material effect on correct signal generation today; it's a growing inefficiency with a trivial fix (bound the probe to the last few days).

findings.title: ATM expiries Redis cache is dead on the live path — payload has no 'rows', so every 60s call from BOTH market_intelligence and the S1 agent deletes and rebuilds it
findings.summary: get_expiries' Redis cache is dead for live_refresh callers: the cached payload never contains a 'rows' key, so the freshness check `_watchlist_rows_are_fresh(cached_payload.get("rows") or [])` always fails and the cache is deleted and rebuilt on every ~60s call from both market_intelligence and the S1 agent — but the rebuild is cheap (per-symbol 300s expiry cache absorbs broker calls), so the cost is one catalog DB query + ~9 Redis GETs per cycle, not broker hammering.
findings.evidence: get_expiries caches a payload containing only expiries/default_expiry/monthly_expiry/... (lines 792-812) — no 'rows' key — yet the cache hit path does `cached_rows = list(cached_payload.get("rows") or [])` then `if live_refresh and not _watchlist_rows_are_fresh(cached_rows): await redis.delete(cache_key)` (lines 683-685); _watchlist_rows_are_fresh([]) returns False because _latest_watchlist_row_time([]) is None (lines 412-416). Callers: market_intelligence_runtime.py:347 and strategy_agent.py:2413, both live_refresh=True every 60s.
findings.signal_impact: The DEFAULT_EXPIRY_TTL cache never serves a live-refresh hit, so the full expiry-ladder rebuild (gather over ~9 representative symbols' broker expiry snapshots + NSE ladder normalization) runs ~2x per minute across the two loops, saved from broker hammering only by the deeper 300s per-symbol cache. That is wasted latency inside both the MI runner (serial-first, delays all trailing lanes) and S1's scan cycle, on every single cycle of the two lanes that generate/feed S1 signals.
findings.fix: Freshness-check expiries payloads on their own age (store an as_of timestamp in the payload and compare against DEFAULT_EXPIRY_TTL / a few minutes) instead of reusing the watchlist-rows freshness helper that can never pass for row-less payloads.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in working tree TradeBot/backend/market_data/atm_watchlist.py: payload built at lines 791-809 has keys expiries/default_expiry/monthly_expiry/... and no 'rows'; hit path lines 682-685 does `cached_rows = list(cached_payload.get("rows") or [])` then `if live_refresh and not _watchlist_rows_are_fresh(cached_rows): await redis.delete(cache_key)`; `_watchlist_rows_are_fresh` (412-416) returns False when `_latest_watchlist_row_time` is None, which it is for []. Callers confirmed live_refresh=True: market_intelligence_runtime.py:347 (refresh_nse_watchlists, run every MI cycle via line 918 `_timed("watchlists", ...)`) and paper_engine/strategy_agent.py:1356/2413 (live_refresh true when broker ready, not local_only). The check is a copy-paste from get_watchlist (line 878) where payloads do carry rows — not deliberate, not covered by baseline items. Downgraded to low: rebuild is Redis/DB-bound (per-symbol snapshot cache at 1606-1611, ex=300 at 1647) so per-cycle waste is milliseconds (worst edge: ensure_fyers_session(force_validate=True) at line 707 when Fyers adapter inactive), and expiry values returned remain correct — no effect on signal correctness. Side effect noted: the shared live-cache read for non-live callers (lines 688-693) also never hits.

findings.title: macd_refined runs synchronous pandas parquet read/concat/write for 217 names on the shared event loop inside its async fan-out
findings.summary: macd_refined's _persist_snapshots does synchronous pandas parquet read/concat/write on the shared event loop (no to_thread) from the async per-name fan-out, but measured blocking is only ~4ms per file today (~60ms worst-case at the 80k-row cap), so it is loop-hygiene debt with negligible current impact on signal generation.
findings.evidence: _process_underlying (an async coroutine gathered under Semaphore(6), lines 344-375) calls `persisted_here += self._persist_snapshots(underlying, rows)` per expiry; _persist_snapshots does blocking `existing = pd.read_parquet(path)`, `pd.concat(...)`, `combined.tail(80_000)`, `combined.to_parquet(tmp, ...)` (lines 272-296) with no asyncio.to_thread. 219 parquet files exist in runtime/macd_refined/volume_tracking, each rewritten fully every 30-min cycle.
findings.signal_impact: All 438 read-modify-write file operations per cycle execute on the single process event loop that also serves the tick router, quote bus, S1 agent loop, and every supervisor runner — each blocking IO slice adds jitter to live tick ingestion and other lanes' awaits, and grows toward the 80k-row cap; this is the same event-loop-blocking pathology already fixed elsewhere with to_thread, and it lengthens the exact macd_refined cycle that head-of-line blocks the scheduler (finding 1).
findings.fix: Wrap _persist_snapshots (and load_tracking on the read side) in asyncio.to_thread, and switch from full-file rewrite to appending only new rows (per-name row cap enforced periodically, not every cycle).
findings.verifier_note: Code claims verified in the working tree: backend/macd_refined/live.py line 355 `persisted_here += self._persist_snapshots(underlying, rows)` inside async `_process_underlying` (gathered under `asyncio.Semaphore(6)`, lines 344-375), and `_persist_snapshots` (272-296) does blocking `pd.read_parquet(path)` → `pd.concat` → `.tail(80_000)` → `to_parquet(tmp)` with zero `to_thread`/`run_in_executor` anywhere in macd_refined/live.py or service.py. Shared-process claim verified: main.py lifespan starts live_candle_store, quote_bus, paper_strategy_agent, and `market_hours_paper_supervisor.start()` (line 217) in one process; the supervisor awaits `macd_refined_service.run_live_cycle()` directly (market_hours_paper_supervisor.py:411, `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=1140.0)`), so all parquet IO lands on the main event loop. 217 files exist in runtime/macd_refined/volume_tracking. HOWEVER, the impact is overstated: I timed the read-modify-write inside the nomadcurie_backend container — files are ~28-1,176 rows (~50KB max, dir total 8.8MB): read 1.9-2.6ms / concat 0.4ms / write 1.3-1.7ms ≈ 4ms per op warm (one 55ms cold outlier). Synthetic worst case at the 80k-row cap: read 12ms / concat 14ms / write 34.5ms = 60ms per op. So per-cycle blocking is ~434 ops × 4ms ≈ 2s in 4ms slices today (≈26s in 60ms slices only after ~200+ trading days of growth), spread across a 30-min-interval cycle whose duration is dominated by broker chain fetches, and well under the quote_bus 150ms coalescing frame. The pattern is real and worth a one-line `asyncio.to_thread` wrap, but it neither corrupts signals nor materially lengthens the macd_refined cycle (1140s budget) at current data sizes — severity low, not medium.

findings.title: Fractal MP parses its entire 39.5MB paper journal to return 8 records, per symbol, every 300s cycle
findings.summary: FMP's list_journal synchronously re-reads and json-parses the entire 39.5MB paper journal (no tail/limit, no executor) to return 8 records, 4x per 300s supervisor cycle — but the measured cost is only ~0.2s per parse (1,393 records), so event-loop impact is ~0.8s/cycle, nowhere near the claimed multi-second blocking or 300s-timeout drift.
findings.evidence: _load_journal opens paper_journal.jsonl and json-parses every line (`for line in handle: ... records.append(json.loads(line))`, lines 712-720) with no tail/limit; live_snapshot calls `analysis["paper_journal"] = await self.paper.list_journal(symbol=normalized, limit=8)` (service.py:631) for each of 4 symbols per supervisor cycle. On-disk file is 39,507,859 bytes and append-only (line 705).
findings.signal_impact: ~40MB of synchronous file IO + JSON parsing (seconds of pure event-loop blocking) runs 4x per 300s cycle inside a runner bounded by the global 300s timeout with no per-symbol budget — as the journal grows unbounded the fmp runner drifts toward its timeout (killed cycle = no FMP signal snapshot that pass), and every parse stalls the shared event loop for all other lanes' signal work.
findings.fix: Read only the file tail (seek from end and parse the last N lines), keep an in-memory ring buffer of recent journal entries appended at write time, and rotate/compact paper_journal.jsonl; move any remaining full-file parse to asyncio.to_thread.
findings.verifier_note: Verified the full chain in the working tree: paper.py:708-721 `_load_journal` does `for line in handle: ... records.append(json.loads(line))` with no limit, called from async `list_journal` (paper.py:58-59) with no executor offload; service.py:631 `analysis["paper_journal"] = await self.paper.list_journal(symbol=normalized, limit=8)` inside live_snapshot; supervisor `_fmp_runner` (market_hours_paper_supervisor.py:183-186) loops all 4 SUPPORTED_SYMBOLS per cycle. File confirmed 39,507,859 bytes at backend/runtime/fractal_market_profile/paper_journal.jsonl. No baseline item covers this. HOWEVER, empirical re-run refutes the magnitude: the file holds only 1,393 records (~28KB each) and a full parse+sort takes 0.20s (measured with the exact same loop), i.e. ~0.8s of event-loop blocking per 300s cycle. Growth is ~0.48MB/day (file spans 2026-04-11 to 2026-07-03), so even a year out it's <1s/parse — the 'seconds of blocking' and 'drifts toward its 300s timeout' impact claims are overstated. Real inefficiency worth a tail-read/deque fix, but immaterial to correct signal generation today, hence severity low, not medium.

findings.title: Runner health persists nowhere across restarts and healthy_runner_count counts never-ran/disabled runners as healthy
findings.summary: Supervisor runner health is memory-only (wiped on restart), healthy_runner_count treats never-ran/disabled runners as healthy, and serialize() omits last_post_close_success_date — so the status API cannot distinguish a fresh/blind supervisor from a healthy one; however, the claimed snapshot_daily duplication is harmless because it idempotently overwrites daily_{date}.json.
findings.evidence: RunnerRuntime (lines 81-93) holds last_started_at/last_success_at/last_error/last_result_meta/last_post_close_success_date as plain dataclass fields with no DB/file persistence anywhere in the module; every field resets to None on container restart (one happened ~1h before this review). get_status line 1050: `healthy_runner_count = sum(1 for item in runners.values() if item.get("last_error") is None)` — a runner that has never run, is disabled, or whose state was wiped by restart counts as healthy. serialize() (lines 117-140) never exposes last_post_close_success_date, so the guaranteed-EOD-pass state is invisible to any monitor.
findings.signal_impact: After any restart the status API shows 10/10 healthy with all timestamps None — indistinguishable from a healthy steady state — so an operator cannot judge whether a lane generated signals today, whether the EOD force-daily pass ran for this session, or how long a lane has been failing. Post-restart, recovery-only catch-ups also re-run and snapshot_daily duplicates, because the dedup state was memory-only. All per-cycle result telemetry (last_result_meta funnels, failure counts) is lost with it.
findings.fix: Persist RunnerRuntime (or at minimum last_success_at, last_error, last_post_close_success_date) to the existing runtime_state DB table on each transition and rehydrate at start(); change healthy_runner_count to require a recent success within k*interval during that runner's market hours; add last_post_close_success_date to serialize().
findings.verifier_note: Verified in TradeBot/backend/core/market_hours_paper_supervisor.py (note: file is under TradeBot/backend/, not backend/). (1) RunnerRuntime (lines 80-93) holds last_started_at/last_success_at/last_error/last_result_meta/last_post_close_success_date as plain dataclass fields; grep of the whole module finds no DB/file/redis persistence of runner state. (2) Line 1050 is exactly as cited: `healthy_runner_count = sum(1 for item in runners.values() if item.get("last_error") is None)` — a disabled or never-ran runner has last_error None and counts healthy. (3) serialize() (lines 117-140) exposes last_started_at/last_success_at/last_finished_at/last_error/last_result_meta but NOT last_post_close_success_date, so the guaranteed-EOD-pass state (post_close_force_daily, lines 742-745) is invisible to monitors. (4) Empirically reproduced the post-restart blindness: `curl http://localhost:8000/api/system/automation-status` returns `"healthy_runner_count": 10` with every runner's last_started_at/last_success_at/last_finished_at = null — exactly '10/10 healthy, all timestamps None'. Corrections to the finder's impact claims: snapshot_daily (paper_trade_recorder.py lines 103-168) recomputes from the events log and overwrites PORTFOLIO_ROOT/daily_{date}.json, so a post-restart re-run is idempotent, not a duplicate; and the post-close catch-up gate (line 50) requires `has_exchange_session("NSE", now.date())`, so nothing spuriously re-fires on this weekend restart — re-runs only occur after a post-15:35 trading-day restart, and the callbacks are the same per-interval cycle functions that run repeatedly anyway. No baseline item covers this; it is an observability gap, not deliberate. Severity lowered to low: it never produces wrong signals, it only blinds the operator to lanes that stop producing them (the same blindness class that let the market_intelligence 300s failure persist, so still worth fixing).

findings.title: Gann lane's paper journal shows exit_reason=None for every closed trade (writes 'close_reason', reads 'exit_reason')
findings.summary: Gann paper journal rows read `p.get("exit_reason")` but closes are stored as `close_reason`, so every one of the 183 closed rows reports exit_reason=None; the actual reason is still present in the embedded `position` payload of each row.
findings.evidence: service.py:172 builds journal rows with `"exit_reason": p.get("exit_reason")`, but agent.py:555 stores the close reason under a different key: `closed.update({... "close_reason": reason, ...})`. No code path ever writes an 'exit_reason' key on gann positions (grep: only these two sites).
findings.signal_impact: The gann lane has 183 closed trades and a suspected exit-discipline bug (time_stop_bars counts 60s scans, not 15m bars, so time stops can fire ~15x early) — but the journal/API that should let you attribute closes to stop/target/time_stop/reversal shows exit_reason=None on every row. Judging whether the lane's exits follow the defined strategy is impossible from its own audit trail; you must diff raw position payloads by hand.
findings.fix: One-line fix: read `p.get("close_reason") or p.get("exit_reason")` in service.py:172 (or rename the write in agent.py:555). Backfill is automatic since payloads already carry close_reason.
findings.verifier_note: Code verified in working tree: TradeBot/backend/gann_tp_delta/service.py:172 builds journal rows with `"exit_reason": p.get("exit_reason")`, while agent.py:555 (`_close_position`) writes `"close_reason": reason`; grep confirms the only `exit_reason` writer is backtest.py:139, a separate path never feeding paper positions. Empirically re-ran the read: GET /api/gann-tp-delta/paper-journal?limit=200 → 183 closed rows, exit_reason=None on all 183, while the nested `position` payload carries close_reason values (gann_stop 28, time_stop 18, gann_target 4 in first 50). No baseline item covers the gann lane. Severity corrected medium→low: this is an audit-trail display bug, not a signal-generation defect — the top-level field is wrong, but each journal row embeds the full position dict (service.py:176 `"position": p`), so exit attribution is one nested key away (no hand-diffing needed), and entries/exits themselves execute on close_reason correctly.

findings.title: Gann paper-book copy drift: agent writes 'close_reason' but the journal/API reads 'exit_reason', so every closed trade's exit reason surfaces as None
findings.summary: Gann paper journal reads a key the agent never writes — service.py:172 `"exit_reason": p.get("exit_reason")` vs agent.py:555 `"close_reason": reason` — so the journal's top-level exit_reason is None on every closed trade; the reason is only recoverable from the nested `position.close_reason` blob.
findings.evidence: gann_tp_delta/agent.py:555 `"close_reason": reason,` in _close_position vs service.py:172 `"exit_reason": p.get("exit_reason"),` in the journal payload — the key never exists on closed positions, a naming drift versus the other lanes' paper books this code was patterned on.
findings.signal_impact: With 183 closes already (heavy churn suspected from the 26-scan time-stop), the one field that says WHY each Gann signal exited is blank in the journal/UI — the paper-mode objective of judging signal correctness per exit cause (time_stop vs gann_stop vs reversal) is blind for this lane, hiding the churn pathology from review.
findings.fix: Read `p.get("close_reason")` in service.py (or write both keys in _close_position); backfill is unnecessary since agent_positions.json retains close_reason.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in code: TradeBot/backend/gann_tp_delta/agent.py:555 `"close_reason": reason,` in _close_position vs TradeBot/backend/gann_tp_delta/service.py:172 `"exit_reason": p.get("exit_reason"),` in paper_journal — no other code sets exit_reason on gann positions (grep over both files). Verified empirically against the live API: GET /api/gann-tp-delta/paper-journal returns closed rows with `exit_reason=None` while `position.close_reason` holds real values (gann_stop, time_stop, gann_stop, gann_stop, time_stop on the 5 latest). No baseline item covers the gann lane. Mitigations that cap severity: (1) each journal row embeds the full position dict, so close_reason is not lost, just not surfaced in the dedicated field; (2) the current Gann frontend (GannTPDeltaWorkspace.tsx) only renders a journal COUNT and reads close_reason from agent-status positions, not the journal's exit_reason — so no user-visible blank today, but any consumer of the journal's documented field (API scripts, future UI) sees None. Zero impact on signal generation itself; it degrades exit-cause reviewability of the lane. Finder's claimed severity (low) stands.

findings.title: macd_refined iv_rank '252-session' window is actually 252 capture-snapshots (~19 sessions at the new 1800s cadence), so the journaled IV-zone mapping labels are computed on the wrong horizon
findings.summary: In macd_refined/live.py:623-624 the "252-session" IV-rank window is applied to per-cycle capture snapshots (~13/session at the 1800s cadence, verified in the live tracking parquet), so journaled iv_rank/iv_zone mapping labels span only ~19 sessions and diverge from the session-based backtest path (signals.py:243); signal acceptance itself is unaffected because iv_gate_enabled=False.
findings.evidence: live.py:622-624: 'iv_hist = atm_rows["iv"].astype(float).map(self._normalize_iv).iloc[:-1]; ivr = iv_rank(iv, iv_hist.tail(iv_window))' where atm_rows is one row per run_cycle capture (captured_at) and iv_window = int(flt_cfg["iv_rank_window_sessions"]) = 252 (config.py:124). At MACD_REFINED_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECONDS=1800 (uncommitted change) there are ~13 captures/session, so .tail(252) spans ~19 sessions, not a 1-year rank; at the old 300s cadence it was ~3 sessions.
findings.signal_impact: IV rank never gates entries (iv_gate_enabled=False, deliberate), but the whole point of recording it is the mapping study — every signals.jsonl row's iv_rank/iv_zone ('cheap'/'rich') label is a short-window rank mislabeled as a 252-session rank, so the eventual cheap-vs-rich edge analysis on this paper lane will be run on systematically wrong labels.
findings.fix: Rank against one IV observation per session (e.g. groupby captured_at.date().last() before .tail(252)), and record the actual number of sessions in the journal row so the mapping analysis can filter under-windowed labels.
findings.verifier_note: Verified in code and live data. live.py:623-624: iv_hist = atm_rows["iv"]...iloc[:-1]; ivr = iv_rank(iv, iv_hist.tail(iv_window)) where atm_rows rows are appended once per run_cycle with captured_at=_utc_now() (live.py:433) and iv_window = flt_cfg["iv_rank_window_sessions"] = 252 (config.py:124). The research path is genuinely session-based: signals.py:239-243 slices a date-indexed atm_iv_history with prior_iv.iloc[-iv_rank_window:]. Empirical check inside the running container (ADANIENT.parquet): 26 capture timestamps/day (13 per expiry), max 39 rows/contract over 3 sessions ≈ 13 snapshots/session, so tail(252) ≈ 19 sessions — finder's math confirmed. No baseline item covers it. Severity lowered to low per the "impact on correct signal generation" criterion: iv_gate_enabled=False (deliberate), so iv_rank never gates entries — only the journaled mapping label is on the wrong horizon; the defect corrupts the future cheap/rich mapping study, not current signals.
